E0336 | v3.7 | BIG | Found Day 56 | Fixed in 5 days | Pi SSH terminal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v3.7/color_detect.py
Error     : sensor_health flags all sensors dead on boot
Terminal  : Pi SSH terminal
  sensor 1: DEAD  sensor 2: DEAD  sensor 3: DEAD
  but all read fine 2 minutes later
WHAT HAPPENED
  The health monitor declared every sensor dead at boot, then two minutes later all of them read fine. The alarm was real - but the verdict was premature.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The health check ran before the sensors finished their initialization sequences. Each sensor takes seconds to warm up (the ToF init alone needs several register delays), and the health monitor's first pass counted the warm-up silence as failures. The check had no grace period, so the boot-time transient was indistinguishable from a real failure.
INVESTIGATION (before the fix)
  - Noticed the pattern: always dead at boot, always fine later
  - Logged the first readings - they arrived after the check window
  - Measured the actual sensor ready time from boot
FIX (took 5 days)
  Fixed by delaying the first health check until 5 seconds after the last sensor reports ready, and adding a warm-up state to the monitor.

E0337 | v3.8 | SMALL | Found Day 57 | Fixed in 1 day | systemd journal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v3.8/blob_config.py
Error     : ToF distance frozen at 0
Terminal  : systemd journal
  $ python3 blob_config.py
  dist: 0, 0, 0, 0, 0 mm
  wall state: UNKNOWN
WHAT HAPPENED
  The distance sensor returned exactly zero on every read. Not an error, not a range value - a perfect, suspicious zero every time.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The VL53L0X boot sequence requires specific register writes with strict timing between them. The init code skipped a required 5ms delay, so the sensor never left its boot state and returned the default register value of 0. The sensor was not broken - it was never initialized. This is why vendor init sequences must be copied exactly, including every delay.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by restoring the complete init sequence with all inter-register delays, and adding a power-on self-check that verifies a non-zero reading.

E0338 | v3.8 | SMALL | Found Day 57 | Fixed in 1 day | systemd journal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v3.8/blob_detect.py
Error     : ToF range error 7 (VL53L1X) floods the log
Terminal  : systemd journal
  $ python3 blob_detect.py
  WARNING: range status 7 (signal fail)
  WARNING: range status 7 (signal fail)
  ... 600 lines/second ...
WHAT HAPPENED
  The console became a waterfall of identical warnings. Within seconds the useful log was buried under thousands of identical lines.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The reflective venue tile produced a weak return echo, so the VL53L1X reported range status 7 (signal fail). The error path logged at full loop rate with no throttle - 600 lines per second is simply the loop rate. Logging is I/O, and I/O at that rate saturated the serial link and starved the control loop of CPU time.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed with a rate limiter that logs the error at most once per 2 seconds and counts the suppressed occurrences, mirroring the I2C fix.

E0339 | v3.8 | SMALL | Found Day 57 | Fixed in 1 day | systemd journal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v3.8/blob_config.py
Error     : Wall state flips every frame
Terminal  : systemd journal
  $ python3 blob_config.py
  state: LEFT WALL, RIGHT WALL, LEFT WALL, ...
  distance jitter +-4cm
WHAT HAPPENED
  The wall-following state changed sides every single frame, making the robot oscillate between two behaviors at 10Hz. The distance was stable within a few centimeters.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The state threshold sat exactly in the middle of the sensor's noise band. A 4cm jitter crossed the threshold in both directions constantly, and the state machine had no hysteresis - no memory of the previous state to suppress rapid toggling. Threshold logic without hysteresis amplifies sensor noise into state oscillation.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by adding a 6cm hysteresis band around the threshold so the state only changes when the distance clearly leaves the current side.

E0340 | v3.8 | SMALL | Found Day 57 | Fixed in 1 day | systemd journal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v3.8/blob_detect.py
Error     : Camera capture returns a black frame
Terminal  : systemd journal
  $ python3 blob_detect.py
  frame mean = 2.1 (near black)
  camera seems dead
WHAT HAPPENED
  The camera test produced almost entirely black frames. The sensor was alive - the log showed it was capturing - but the image was dark.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The camera was still in preview mode with auto-exposure running when the first capture happened. The capture raced the exposure settling, so the frame froze before the sensor adapted to the light. A camera is not instantly ready: after start, the auto-exposure algorithm needs several frames to converge, and a read immediately after init captures the un-converged state.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by forcing a 500ms settle delay after camera start and discarding the first three frames before using any image.

E0341 | v3.8 | SMALL | Found Day 57 | Fixed in 1 day | systemd journal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v3.8/blob_config.py
Error     : MPU6050 WHO_AM_I mismatch 0x00
Terminal  : systemd journal
  $ python3 blob_config.py
  WHO_AM_I = 0x00 (expected 0x68)
  IMU not found on bus
WHAT HAPPENED
  The IMU log script reported the sensor was absent even though it was wired and powered. The address check failed on the very first register read.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The MPU6050 answers at 0x68 or 0x69 depending on the AD0 pin. With AD0 floating, the pin read as high at power-up and the chip moved to 0x69, while the code only probed 0x68. WHO_AM_I returning 0x00 means the device never even acknowledged - the wrong address was being addressed, so the chip stayed silent.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by pulling AD0 to ground with a resistor and adding a bus scan that discovers the device address instead of assuming it.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
E0342 | v3.8 | SMALL | Found Day 57 | Fixed in 1 day | systemd journal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v3.8/blob_detect.py
Error     : Calibration JSON has no 'gyro_offset' key
Terminal  : systemd journal
  $ python3 blob_detect.py
  KeyError: 'gyro_offset'
    File "blob_detect.py", line 27, in load_calib
WHAT HAPPENED
  The IMU driver crashed at startup reading its calibration file. The file existed and looked complete - the schema was the problem.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The calibration file was produced by an older calibration script that stored the fields under different names. The loader used strict key access (calib['gyro_offset']) so a renamed key raised KeyError instantly. There was no schema version in the file and no migration path, so old and new files were indistinguishable until load time.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by adding a schema version field, a default fallback for missing keys, and regenerating imu_calib.json with the new format.

E0343 | v3.8 | SMALL | Found Day 57 | Fixed in 1 day | systemd journal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v3.8/blob_config.py
Error     : Complementary filter alpha out of bounds
Terminal  : systemd journal
  $ python3 blob_config.py
  filter_config.json: alpha=1.7
  pitch follows raw accel with spikes
WHAT HAPPENED
  The live pitch plot showed violent spikes as if the gyro was ignored. The filter ran, but the numbers made no physical sense.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The complementary filter weights gyro integration by alpha and the accelerometer by (1 - alpha). With alpha=1.7 the accelerometer weight became -0.7, so the filter was actively amplifying accelerometer noise instead of suppressing it. A typo in filter_config.json wrote 1.7 instead of 0.7, and nothing validated the config against the [0,1] domain the math requires.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by clamping alpha at load time and adding a config validator that rejects values outside [0,1] with a readable error.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
E0344 | v3.8 | SMALL | Found Day 57 | Fixed in 1 day | systemd journal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v3.8/blob_detect.py
Error     : Magnetometer saturates near the drive motors
Terminal  : systemd journal
  $ python3 blob_detect.py
  mag: x=+32767 y=-32767 z=+1024
  heading: jumping 0..359
WHAT HAPPENED
  The heading readout became random noise whenever the throttle rose. At standstill it was fine; the moment the motors spun, the compass went mad.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The QMC5883L's ADC saturated at its ±32767 output limits, which means the magnetic field at the sensor exceeded its measurement range. The motor current creates a strong magnetic field a few centimeters away, and at 2cm distance the field strength is comparable to the Earth's field the sensor is trying to measure. Saturated ADC values are not noise - they are clipped, which corrupts the heading completely.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by moving the sensor 5cm from the motor wiring, adding hard-iron offset calibration, and masking the heading while the throttle exceeds a threshold.

E0348 | v3.8 | BIG | Found Day 58 | Fixed in 5 days | ESP32 serial monitor
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v3.8/blob_detect.py
Error     : MPU6050 FIFO overflows after 30s
Terminal  : ESP32 serial monitor
  E (30000) mpu6050: FIFO overflow (2048 bytes)
  gyro data: stale frames
WHAT HAPPENED
  Every 30 seconds the gyro stream glitched. The FIFO overflow error appeared exactly at the 30-second mark, every run, like clockwork.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The MPU6050 buffers samples in an internal 2048-byte FIFO, and the reader drained it at 50Hz while the sensor produced at 100Hz. The drain rate was half the fill rate, so the FIFO filled exactly at the overflow point - 30 seconds at these rates. The periodic glitch was the FIFO resetting, and the periodic timing was the giveaway: a hardware error would not repeat on a precise schedule.
INVESTIGATION (before the fix)
  - Noticed the glitch was perfectly periodic - rate mismatch, not hardware
  - Computed fill vs drain rates from the registers
  - Confirmed the FIFO level grew linearly between overflows
FIX (took 5 days)
  Fixed by draining the FIFO at 200Hz (twice the sensor rate) and monitoring the FIFO level register as a health metric.

----------------------------------------------------------------------

Error     : IMU calibration accepted garbage data
Terminal  : Pi SSH terminal
  $ python3 calibrate_imu.py
  collecting... done (120 samples)
  gyro bias: 1.34 deg/s (was 0.01)
  result: worse than before
WHAT HAPPENED
  The calibration tool ran 'successfully' but produced a bias 100x worse than the previous value. The tool had no way to know the robot was being bumped while it collected.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  Calibration is a statistical estimate: it averages samples to find the bias. If the robot moves during collection, the samples contain real motion plus bias, and the average is corrupted. The tool trusted its input completely - it never checked whether the sensor was still, because stillness was an assumption, not a measurement. Garbage in, garbage out, with a success message on top.
INVESTIGATION (before the fix)
  - Re-ran the calibration with the robot untouched - bias returned to 0.01
  - Compared the sample variance between the two runs
  - Found the bump event in the session log by timestamp
FIX (took 5 days)
  Fixed by computing the sample variance before accepting the result and requiring the robot to be still, with a 'movement detected' warning when the variance is too high.

E0361 | v4.0 | SMALL | Found Day 61 | Fixed in 1 day | Pi SSH terminal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v4.0/config.py
Error     : Lane offset jumps by a full lane width
Terminal  : Pi SSH terminal
  $ python3 config.py
  offset: 0.02 -> 0.47 (one frame)
  lane lost for 0.3s
WHAT HAPPENED
  The lane offset jumped from center to a full lane width away in a single frame. The steering twitched violently and then recovered.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  When the line had a gap, the detector locked onto a neighboring line - the other lane's edge or a shadow - and reported it as the track line. The offset filter had no state, so one wrong frame was trusted completely for one control tick. Vision systems without temporal consistency treat every frame as a fresh truth, which amplifies single-frame errors.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by tracking the last-good line position and snapping back to it when the new detection is more than a lane-width away.

E0362 | v4.0 | SMALL | Found Day 61 | Fixed in 1 day | Pi SSH terminal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v4.0/lane_detect.py
Error     : Camera resolution mismatch with calibration
Terminal  : Pi SSH terminal
  $ python3 lane_detect.py
  cv2.error: (-215:Assertion failed)
  !src.empty() in function 'undistort'
WHAT HAPPENED
  The camera pipeline crashed on undistort. The calibration data loaded fine, so the mismatch was invisible until the function call.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The camera opened at 1280x720 but the calibration was done at 640x480. cv2.undistort requires the image size to match the camera matrix, and the mismatch triggered OpenCV's internal assertion. The two settings lived in different config files that were never cross-checked - one for the camera driver, one for the calibration loader.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by forcing both to the same resolution in camera_config.py and adding a boot check that compares the frame size with the calibration size.

E0363 | v4.0 | SMALL | Found Day 61 | Fixed in 1 day | Pi SSH terminal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v4.0/config.py
Error     : HSV lower bound bigger than upper bound
Terminal  : Pi SSH terminal
  $ python3 config.py
  ValueError: lower should be smaller than upper
    File "config.py", line 34, in detect
WHAT HAPPENED
  The red pillar detector crashed the first time it processed a real frame. The color range that worked in tests was rejected by OpenCV.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  Red hue wraps around the HSV cylinder: red is both 0-10 and 170-180. Writing it as one continuous range (170..10) is invalid because lower > upper, which cv2.inRange rejects with a ValueError. The wrapper range is a conceptual mistake - the hue circle has no beginning, so the mask must be built from two disjoint ranges and OR-ed together.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by splitting the red range into two masks (0-10 and 170-180) and OR-ing the results, with a comment explaining the hue wrap.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
E0364 | v4.0 | SMALL | Found Day 61 | Fixed in 1 day | Pi SSH terminal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v4.0/lane_detect.py
Error     : ZeroDivisionError in distance estimate
Terminal  : Pi SSH terminal
  $ python3 lane_detect.py
    File "lane_detect.py", line 58, in estimate
      dist = known_h / h
  ZeroDivisionError: float division by zero
WHAT HAPPENED
  The pillar distance estimator crashed mid-frame, not at startup. The contour had been found, but its height was zero.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The detector found a contour but the color filter had removed every interior pixel, leaving a height of zero. The distance formula assumes a valid height; dividing by zero raised ZeroDivisionError. This is a data-quality failure: the pipeline did not validate its input before applying the pinhole model, so a degenerate contour crashed the math instead of being skipped.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by skipping contours smaller than 5 pixels and returning 'unknown' instead of crashing when the height is invalid.

E0365 | v4.0 | SMALL | Found Day 61 | Fixed in 1 day | Pi SSH terminal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v4.0/config.py
Error     : Pillar detected at every frame edge
Terminal  : Pi SSH terminal
  $ python3 config.py
  pillar: (5, 20)  pillar: (610, 20)  ...
  false positives on the wall
WHAT HAPPENED
  The detector reported pillars at fixed screen positions in every frame. The track walls were being detected as red pillars.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The wall's edge pixels had similar HSV values to the pillar under the venue lighting, and the detector only matched color - it never checked size or shape. Any red-ish region, including a wall edge, passed the filter. A single-channel color test is necessary but not sufficient; without area and aspect-ratio constraints every similarly colored region is a candidate.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by adding a minimum area check and an aspect-ratio gate, and by masking the bottom 15% of the frame where the wall always appears.

E0366 | v4.0 | SMALL | Found Day 61 | Fixed in 1 day | Pi SSH terminal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v4.0/lane_detect.py
Error     : Red and pink pillars are confused
Terminal  : Pi SSH terminal
  $ python3 lane_detect.py
  color=red  (was pink)
  confusion at hue 168-175
WHAT HAPPENED
  The color classifier called a pink pillar red. The two classes were defined by hue bands that overlapped, so the classification was ambiguous by construction.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  Pink and red differ in saturation and lightness, not much in hue. The classifier only used hue, so any pixel in the overlapping 168-175 band was claimed by both classes. Classifying colors by a single channel cannot separate classes that are distinct in a different channel - the feature space was too small for the problem.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by narrowing the red band and adding a saturation threshold of 90, since pink has measurably lower saturation than the official red.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
E0367 | v4.0 | SMALL | Found Day 61 | Fixed in 1 day | Pi SSH terminal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v4.0/config.py
Error     : Free space is NaN after a corner
Terminal  : Pi SSH terminal
  $ python3 config.py
  free_space: nan
  corner left: nan
WHAT HAPPENED
  The free-space estimate became NaN at every corner. The robot continued driving, but the planner received garbage for the entire turn.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  While angling through a corner, the ToF reported 0mm (out of range), and the fusion code divided by that reading to normalize the estimate. NaN is infectious: one 0/0 poisons every downstream calculation, and because NaN comparisons are all false, no safety check could catch it. The corner is exactly where the sensor points at a gap, so this happened on every lap.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by replacing non-finite values with the sensor's max range and adding a validation pass that rejects NaN before fusion.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
E0368 | v4.0 | SMALL | Found Day 61 | Fixed in 1 day | Pi SSH terminal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v4.0/lane_detect.py
Error     : Corner detection misses 180-degree turns
Terminal  : Pi SSH terminal
  $ python3 lane_detect.py
  corner count = 0 after full lap
  expected 4 corners
WHAT HAPPENED
  The lap trace showed zero corners even though the robot clearly turned four times. The detector only watched distance, and the hairpin was too smooth.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The corner detector used a distance-only signature: it watched the wall distance change. A 180-degree turn made with a wide arc changes distance slowly and smoothly, so the slope never exceeded the trigger threshold. The signature was chosen for right-angle corners, and a different geometry produced a different signature entirely - one feature cannot describe all corner shapes.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by adding the heading-change signature from the IMU, and requiring both signatures for a confirmed corner.

E0369 | v4.0 | BIG | Found Day 62 | Fixed in 2 days | Pi SSH terminal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v4.0/config.py
Error     : Free space wrongly reports a corridor
Terminal  : Pi SSH terminal
  free space: 0.9m corridor detected
  reality: 0.4m gap
WHAT HAPPENED
  The free-space module reported a 0.9m corridor where only a 0.4m gap existed. The robot planned to drive through a space it could not fit through.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The fusion code averaged the ToF wall distance with the camera gap estimate. Averaging is only valid when both measurements describe the same quantity; here one sensor measured the wall and the other measured the gap, and the mean produced a number that matched neither reality. The 'corridor' was a pure artifact of mixing incompatible measurements.
INVESTIGATION (before the fix)
  - Reproduced the false corridor with the ToF and camera both active
  - Logged each sensor's raw value - they disagreed fundamentally
  - Tested taking the minimum instead of the mean - correct result
FIX (took 2 days)
  Fixed by taking the minimum of the two estimates (the conservative choice for a gap) and by storing the source of each free-space measurement.

E0370 | v4.0 | BIG | Found Day 62 | Fixed in 3 days | Pi SSH terminal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v4.0/lane_detect.py
Error     : Pillar tracking loses the pillar at 2m/s
Terminal  : Pi SSH terminal
  tracked: 10 frames, lost at frame 11
  pillar reappears 20 frames later
WHAT HAPPENED
  The tracker followed the pillar perfectly at low speed, then lost it the moment the robot accelerated. It always lost it at the same point on the approach.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The tracker searched a fixed window around the last known position. At 2m/s the pillar moves several pixels between frames, and once it left the search window the tracker had nothing to lock onto. The search window size was tuned for walking speed, not race speed. A tracker with no motion model is only as fast as its window is wide.
INVESTIGATION (before the fix)
  - Measured the pillar's inter-frame displacement at speed
  - Found the displacement exceeded the search window
  - Predicted the position with odometry - tracking held
FIX (took 3 days)
  Fixed by predicting the search window center with the odometry velocity before matching, and widening the window proportional to speed.

E0371 | v4.0 | BIG | Found Day 62 | Fixed in 4 days | Pi SSH terminal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v4.0/config.py
Error     : Pillar never detected under venue lights
Terminal  : Pi SSH terminal
  pillars: 0 found (12 frames)
  HSV test on the phone: 0 found
  color bands all wrong
WHAT HAPPENED
  The pillar detector found nothing for the entire morning. The same code had detected pillars perfectly in the lab the day before.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The morning sun changed the color temperature of the light, shifting every color's HSV values. Fixed HSV bands are calibrated for one lighting condition; a different light source moves the same physical color to a different point in HSV space. Vision systems are lighting-dependent by nature - the color of light is part of the measurement, not a nuisance term.
INVESTIGATION (before the fix)
  - Confirmed detection worked in the lab under fluorescent light
  - Sampled the pillar's HSV values under the morning sun
  - Compared the sampled values with the configured bands
FIX (took 4 days)
  Fixed by re-running the color calibration on the venue floor at the same time of day as the competition, and by making the calibration tool part of the morning routine.

E0372 | v4.0 | BIG | Found Day 62 | Fixed in 5 days | Pi SSH terminal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v4.0/lane_detect.py
Error     : Visual odometry scale explodes after a turn
Terminal  : Pi SSH terminal
  vo scale: 1.0 -> 9.3
  pose jumps 0.4m per frame
WHAT HAPPENED
  After the 90-degree turn, the visual odometry started reporting absurd distances - the pose jumped 0.4 meters per frame while the robot moved a few centimeters.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  Visual odometry estimates motion from feature point displacement and derives the scale from the baseline between frames. After a sharp turn, feature matching lost the reference set and re-matched against a new baseline, and the scale estimate - unconstrained by any absolute reference - diverged. Monocular scale is only observable while the same features persist; a turn breaks that chain.
INVESTIGATION (before the fix)
  - Plotted the scale factor over time - flat before the turn, exploding after
  - Counted matched features across the turn - dropped below the threshold
  - Replayed the turn with forced re-initialization - problem vanished
FIX (took 5 days)
  Fixed by re-initializing the baseline when the matched feature count drops below 20, and by clamping the scale factor to a physically plausible range.

E0388 | v4.2 | SMALL | Found Day 65 | Fixed in 1 day | ESP32 serial monitor

File      : history/v4.2/test_free_space.py
Error     : Red and pink pillars are confused
Terminal  : ESP32 serial monitor
  $ python3 test_free_space.py
  color=red  (was pink)
  confusion at hue 168-175
WHAT HAPPENED
  The color classifier called a pink pillar red. The two classes were defined by hue bands that overlapped, so the classification was ambiguous by construction.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  Pink and red differ in saturation and lightness, not much in hue. The classifier only used hue, so any pixel in the overlapping 168-175 band was claimed by both classes. Classifying colors by a single channel cannot separate classes that are distinct in a different channel - the feature space was too small for the problem.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by narrowing the red band and adding a saturation threshold of 90, since pink has measurably lower saturation than the official red.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
E0389 | v4.2 | SMALL | Found Day 65 | Fixed in 1 day | ESP32 serial monitor
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v4.2/free_space.py
Error     : Free space is NaN after a corner
Terminal  : ESP32 serial monitor
  $ python3 free_space.py
  free_space: nan
  corner left: nan
WHAT HAPPENED
  The free-space estimate became NaN at every corner. The robot continued driving, but the planner received garbage for the entire turn.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  While angling through a corner, the ToF reported 0mm (out of range), and the fusion code divided by that reading to normalize the estimate. NaN is infectious: one 0/0 poisons every downstream calculation, and because NaN comparisons are all false, no safety check could catch it. The corner is exactly where the sensor points at a gap, so this happened on every lap.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by replacing non-finite values with the sensor's max range and adding a validation pass that rejects NaN before fusion.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
E0390 | v4.2 | SMALL | Found Day 65 | Fixed in 1 day | ESP32 serial monitor
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v4.2/test_free_space.py
Error     : Corner detection misses 180-degree turns
Terminal  : ESP32 serial monitor
  $ python3 test_free_space.py
  corner count = 0 after full lap
  expected 4 corners
WHAT HAPPENED
  The lap trace showed zero corners even though the robot clearly turned four times. The detector only watched distance, and the hairpin was too smooth.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The corner detector used a distance-only signature: it watched the wall distance change. A 180-degree turn made with a wide arc changes distance slowly and smoothly, so the slope never exceeded the trigger threshold. The signature was chosen for right-angle corners, and a different geometry produced a different signature entirely - one feature cannot describe all corner shapes.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by adding the heading-change signature from the IMU, and requiring both signatures for a confirmed corner.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
E0391 | v4.2 | SMALL | Found Day 65 | Fixed in 1 day | ESP32 serial monitor
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v4.2/free_space.py
Error     : Lane offset jumps by a full lane width
Terminal  : ESP32 serial monitor
  $ python3 free_space.py
  offset: 0.02 -> 0.47 (one frame)
  lane lost for 0.3s
WHAT HAPPENED
  The lane offset jumped from center to a full lane width away in a single frame. The steering twitched violently and then recovered.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  When the line had a gap, the detector locked onto a neighboring line - the other lane's edge or a shadow - and reported it as the track line. The offset filter had no state, so one wrong frame was trusted completely for one control tick. Vision systems without temporal consistency treat every frame as a fresh truth, which amplifies single-frame errors.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by tracking the last-good line position and snapping back to it when the new detection is more than a lane-width away.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
E0392 | v4.2 | SMALL | Found Day 65 | Fixed in 1 day | ESP32 serial monitor
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v4.2/test_free_space.py
Error     : Camera resolution mismatch with calibration
Terminal  : ESP32 serial monitor
  $ python3 test_free_space.py
  cv2.error: (-215:Assertion failed)
  !src.empty() in function 'undistort'
WHAT HAPPENED
  The camera pipeline crashed on undistort. The calibration data loaded fine, so the mismatch was invisible until the function call.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The camera opened at 1280x720 but the calibration was done at 640x480. cv2.undistort requires the image size to match the camera matrix, and the mismatch triggered OpenCV's internal assertion. The two settings lived in different config files that were never cross-checked - one for the camera driver, one for the calibration loader.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by forcing both to the same resolution in camera_config.py and adding a boot check that compares the frame size with the calibration size.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
E0393 | v4.2 | BIG | Found Day 66 | Fixed in 2 days | Pi SSH terminal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v4.2/free_space.py
Error     : Pillar never detected under venue lights
Terminal  : Pi SSH terminal
  pillars: 0 found (12 frames)
  HSV test on the phone: 0 found
  color bands all wrong
WHAT HAPPENED
  The pillar detector found nothing for the entire morning. The same code had detected pillars perfectly in the lab the day before.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The morning sun changed the color temperature of the light, shifting every color's HSV values. Fixed HSV bands are calibrated for one lighting condition; a different light source moves the same physical color to a different point in HSV space. Vision systems are lighting-dependent by nature - the color of light is part of the measurement, not a nuisance term.
INVESTIGATION (before the fix)
  - Confirmed detection worked in the lab under fluorescent light
  - Sampled the pillar's HSV values under the morning sun
  - Compared the sampled values with the configured bands
FIX (took 2 days)
  Fixed by re-running the color calibration on the venue floor at the same time of day as the competition, and by making the calibration tool part of the morning routine.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
E0394 | v4.2 | BIG | Found Day 66 | Fixed in 3 days | Pi SSH terminal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v4.2/test_free_space.py
Error     : Visual odometry scale explodes after a turn
Terminal  : Pi SSH terminal
  vo scale: 1.0 -> 9.3
  pose jumps 0.4m per frame
WHAT HAPPENED
  After the 90-degree turn, the visual odometry started reporting absurd distances - the pose jumped 0.4 meters per frame while the robot moved a few centimeters.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  Visual odometry estimates motion from feature point displacement and derives the scale from the baseline between frames. After a sharp turn, feature matching lost the reference set and re-matched against a new baseline, and the scale estimate - unconstrained by any absolute reference - diverged. Monocular scale is only observable while the same features persist; a turn breaks that chain.
INVESTIGATION (before the fix)
  - Plotted the scale factor over time - flat before the turn, exploding after
  - Counted matched features across the turn - dropped below the threshold
  - Replayed the turn with forced re-initialization - problem vanished
FIX (took 3 days)
  Fixed by re-initializing the baseline when the matched feature count drops below 20, and by clamping the scale factor to a physically plausible range.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
E0395 | v4.2 | BIG | Found Day 66 | Fixed in 4 days | Pi SSH terminal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v4.2/free_space.py
Error     : False pillar detection passes the wrong side
Terminal  : Pi SSH terminal
  pillar: DETECTED (x=300)
  actual pillar: on the right
  robot went left -> round ends
WHAT HAPPENED
  The robot steered around a 'pillar' that did not exist, passed the real pillar on the wrong side, and ended the round. One false positive cost the whole run.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  A red sponsor sign on the wall matched the pillar filter's color and shape gates, so the detector committed to it. Detection gates are filters, not guarantees: the sign genuinely looked like a pillar in every feature the code checked. The detector had no cross-sensor confirmation - the ToF was available and would have shown no pillar at that location, but nothing asked it.
INVESTIGATION (before the fix)
  - Replayed the round and confirmed the false positive in the video
  - Checked the sign's HSV - inside the pillar bands exactly
  - Verified the ToF had a clear reading at that moment - no pillar
FIX (took 4 days)
  Fixed by adding a ToF distance gate: a detection without a matching distance reading is treated as a candidate, not a pillar.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
E0396 | v4.2 | BIG | Found Day 66 | Fixed in 5 days | Pi SSH terminal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v4.2/test_free_space.py
Error     : Corner detector fires on every shadow
Terminal  : Pi SSH terminal
  corner at 23%, corner at 41%, corner at 68%
  4 corners on a straight
WHAT HAPPENED
  The corner detector reported four corners on a perfectly straight run. Every shadow on the track was being counted as a corner.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The detector's signature was a dark region interrupting the line - and a shadow is exactly that. Shadows are darker than the line, so any luminance-based signature confuses them. The detector had no heading information, so it could not know the robot never turned. A corner is an event in the robot's motion, not in the image; using only image features guaranteed the failure.
INVESTIGATION (before the fix)
  - Overlaid the corner events on the video - each matched a shadow
  - Checked the IMU heading at those moments - no turn occurred
  - Confirmed the signature was purely visual
FIX (took 5 days)
  Fixed by requiring a heading change of at least 45 degrees from the IMU to confirm a corner, demoting image-only detections to candidates.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
E0397 | v4.3 | SMALL | Found Day 67 | Fixed in 1 day | Windows CMD
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v4.3/corner_detect.py
Error     : ZeroDivisionError in distance estimate
Terminal  : Windows CMD
  $ python3 corner_detect.py
    File "corner_detect.py", line 58, in estimate
      dist = known_h / h
  ZeroDivisionError: float division by zero
WHAT HAPPENED
  The pillar distance estimator crashed mid-frame, not at startup. The contour had been found, but its height was zero.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The detector found a contour but the color filter had removed every interior pixel, leaving a height of zero. The distance formula assumes a valid height; dividing by zero raised ZeroDivisionError. This is a data-quality failure: the pipeline did not validate its input before applying the pinhole model, so a degenerate contour crashed the math instead of being skipped.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by skipping contours smaller than 5 pixels and returning 'unknown' instead of crashing when the height is invalid.

E0398 | v4.3 | SMALL | Found Day 67 | Fixed in 1 day | Windows CMD
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v4.3/imu_driver.py
Error     : Pillar detected at every frame edge
Terminal  : Windows CMD
  $ python3 imu_driver.py
  pillar: (5, 20)  pillar: (610, 20)  ...
  false positives on the wall
WHAT HAPPENED
  The detector reported pillars at fixed screen positions in every frame. The track walls were being detected as red pillars.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The wall's edge pixels had similar HSV values to the pillar under the venue lighting, and the detector only matched color - it never checked size or shape. Any red-ish region, including a wall edge, passed the filter. A single-channel color test is necessary but not sufficient; without area and aspect-ratio constraints every similarly colored region is a candidate.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by adding a minimum area check and an aspect-ratio gate, and by masking the bottom 15% of the frame where the wall always appears.

E0404 | v4.3 | SMALL | Found Day 67 | Fixed in 1 day | Windows CMD
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v4.3/imu_driver.py
Error     : HSV lower bound bigger than upper bound
Terminal  : Windows CMD
  $ python3 imu_driver.py
  ValueError: lower should be smaller than upper
    File "imu_driver.py", line 34, in detect
WHAT HAPPENED
  The red pillar detector crashed the first time it processed a real frame. The color range that worked in tests was rejected by OpenCV.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  Red hue wraps around the HSV cylinder: red is both 0-10 and 170-180. Writing it as one continuous range (170..10) is invalid because lower > upper, which cv2.inRange rejects with a ValueError. The wrapper range is a conceptual mistake - the hue circle has no beginning, so the mask must be built from two disjoint ranges and OR-ed together.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by splitting the red range into two masks (0-10 and 170-180) and OR-ing the results, with a comment explaining the hue wrap.

----------------------------------------------------------------------

E0408 | v4.3 | BIG | Found Day 68 | Fixed in 5 days | Pi SSH terminal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v4.3/imu_driver.py
Error     : Lane detection flips to the left wall at 12:00
Terminal  : Pi SSH terminal
  lane: right (12:01), left (12:00), right (12:02)
  sun angle change broke thresholds
WHAT HAPPENED
  Every day at noon the lane detection started flip-flopping between the right lane and the left wall. It always recovered an hour later - the timing was the clue.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The sun moved across the window and changed the light geometry. Fixed color thresholds that worked in the morning and afternoon failed exactly when the sun angle shifted the white balance. The thresholds were static, but the illumination was dynamic, so the system could only be correct for part of the day. The daily repeatability proved the cause was environmental, not random.
INVESTIGATION (before the fix)
  - Noticed the error was perfectly time-correlated across days
  - Captured the failing frames - the white balance had shifted
  - Compared the histogram with the threshold band
FIX (took 5 days)
  Fixed by switching to adaptive thresholding (Otsu on the value channel) so the detector re-calibrates to the current illumination every frame.

      dist = known_h / h
  ZeroDivisionError: float division by zero
WHAT HAPPENED
  The pillar distance estimator crashed mid-frame, not at startup. The contour had been found, but its height was zero.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The detector found a contour but the color filter had removed every interior pixel, leaving a height of zero. The distance formula assumes a valid height; dividing by zero raised ZeroDivisionError. This is a data-quality failure: the pipeline did not validate its input before applying the pinhole model, so a degenerate contour crashed the math instead of being skipped.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by skipping contours smaller than 5 pixels and returning 'unknown' instead of crashing when the height is invalid.

E0417 | v4.4 | BIG | Found Day 70 | Fixed in 2 days | Pi SSH terminal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v4.4/red_pillar.py
Error     : False pillar detection passes the wrong side
Terminal  : Pi SSH terminal
  pillar: DETECTED (x=300)
  actual pillar: on the right
  robot went left -> round ends
WHAT HAPPENED
  The robot steered around a 'pillar' that did not exist, passed the real pillar on the wrong side, and ended the round. One false positive cost the whole run.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  A red sponsor sign on the wall matched the pillar filter's color and shape gates, so the detector committed to it. Detection gates are filters, not guarantees: the sign genuinely looked like a pillar in every feature the code checked. The detector had no cross-sensor confirmation - the ToF was available and would have shown no pillar at that location, but nothing asked it.
INVESTIGATION (before the fix)
  - Replayed the round and confirmed the false positive in the video
  - Checked the sign's HSV - inside the pillar bands exactly
  - Verified the ToF had a clear reading at that moment - no pillar
FIX (took 2 days)
  Fixed by adding a ToF distance gate: a detection without a matching distance reading is treated as a candidate, not a pillar.

E0418 | v4.4 | BIG | Found Day 70 | Fixed in 3 days | Pi SSH terminal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v4.4/red_pillar.py
Error     : Corner detector fires on every shadow
Terminal  : Pi SSH terminal
  corner at 23%, corner at 41%, corner at 68%
  4 corners on a straight
WHAT HAPPENED
  The corner detector reported four corners on a perfectly straight run. Every shadow on the track was being counted as a corner.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The detector's signature was a dark region interrupting the line - and a shadow is exactly that. Shadows are darker than the line, so any luminance-based signature confuses them. The detector had no heading information, so it could not know the robot never turned. A corner is an event in the robot's motion, not in the image; using only image features guaranteed the failure.
INVESTIGATION (before the fix)
  - Overlaid the corner events on the video - each matched a shadow
  - Checked the IMU heading at those moments - no turn occurred
  - Confirmed the signature was purely visual
FIX (took 3 days)
  Fixed by requiring a heading change of at least 45 degrees from the IMU to confirm a corner, demoting image-only detections to candidates.

E0419 | v4.4 | BIG | Found Day 70 | Fixed in 4 days | Pi SSH terminal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v4.4/red_pillar.py
Error     : Lane detection flips to the left wall at 12:00
Terminal  : Pi SSH terminal
  lane: right (12:01), left (12:00), right (12:02)
  sun angle change broke thresholds
WHAT HAPPENED
  Every day at noon the lane detection started flip-flopping between the right lane and the left wall. It always recovered an hour later - the timing was the clue.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The sun moved across the window and changed the light geometry. Fixed color thresholds that worked in the morning and afternoon failed exactly when the sun angle shifted the white balance. The thresholds were static, but the illumination was dynamic, so the system could only be correct for part of the day. The daily repeatability proved the cause was environmental, not random.
INVESTIGATION (before the fix)
  - Noticed the error was perfectly time-correlated across days
  - Captured the failing frames - the white balance had shifted
  - Compared the histogram with the threshold band
FIX (took 4 days)
  Fixed by switching to adaptive thresholding (Otsu on the value channel) so the detector re-calibrates to the current illumination every frame.

E0420 | v4.4 | BIG | Found Day 70 | Fixed in 5 days | Pi SSH terminal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v4.4/red_pillar.py
Error     : Green pillar invisible on the grass backdrop
Terminal  : Pi SSH terminal
  green pillar: 0 pixels
  backdrop hue matches the pillar
WHAT HAPPENED
  The green pillar detector found zero pixels while the pillar sat in plain view. The practice field behind it was green too.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The green pillar and the green grass shared the same hue range, so the color filter selected the entire background and the detector's foreground logic found nothing - the pillar was invisible because the background was identical. Color is not a sufficient feature when the background shares the color; the detector needed a feature the backdrop lacks, such as the pillar's frame edges.
INVESTIGATION (before the fix)
  - Sampled the pillar and grass hues - nearly identical
  - Tested the detector against a neutral background - worked
  - Confirmed the failure was contrast, not calibration
FIX (took 5 days)
  Fixed by detecting the red frame around the pillar as the primary signature, and using the green fill only as confirmation.

E0421 | v4.5 | SMALL | Found Day 71 | Fixed in 1 day | VS Code terminal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v4.5/green_pillar.py
Error     : Red and pink pillars are confused
Terminal  : VS Code terminal
  $ python3 green_pillar.py
  color=red  (was pink)
  confusion at hue 168-175
WHAT HAPPENED
  The color classifier called a pink pillar red. The two classes were defined by hue bands that overlapped, so the classification was ambiguous by construction.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  Pink and red differ in saturation and lightness, not much in hue. The classifier only used hue, so any pixel in the overlapping 168-175 band was claimed by both classes. Classifying colors by a single channel cannot separate classes that are distinct in a different channel - the feature space was too small for the problem.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by narrowing the red band and adding a saturation threshold of 90, since pink has measurably lower saturation than the official red.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
E0422 | v4.5 | SMALL | Found Day 71 | Fixed in 1 day | VS Code terminal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v4.5/green_pillar.py
Error     : Free space is NaN after a corner
Terminal  : VS Code terminal
  $ python3 green_pillar.py
  free_space: nan
  corner left: nan
WHAT HAPPENED
  The free-space estimate became NaN at every corner. The robot continued driving, but the planner received garbage for the entire turn.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  While angling through a corner, the ToF reported 0mm (out of range), and the fusion code divided by that reading to normalize the estimate. NaN is infectious: one 0/0 poisons every downstream calculation, and because NaN comparisons are all false, no safety check could catch it. The corner is exactly where the sensor points at a gap, so this happened on every lap.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by replacing non-finite values with the sensor's max range and adding a validation pass that rejects NaN before fusion.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
E0423 | v4.5 | SMALL | Found Day 71 | Fixed in 1 day | VS Code terminal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v4.5/green_pillar.py
Error     : Corner detection misses 180-degree turns
Terminal  : VS Code terminal
  $ python3 green_pillar.py
  corner count = 0 after full lap
  expected 4 corners
WHAT HAPPENED
  The lap trace showed zero corners even though the robot clearly turned four times. The detector only watched distance, and the hairpin was too smooth.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The corner detector used a distance-only signature: it watched the wall distance change. A 180-degree turn made with a wide arc changes distance slowly and smoothly, so the slope never exceeded the trigger threshold. The signature was chosen for right-angle corners, and a different geometry produced a different signature entirely - one feature cannot describe all corner shapes.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by adding the heading-change signature from the IMU, and requiring both signatures for a confirmed corner.

E0424 | v4.5 | SMALL | Found Day 71 | Fixed in 1 day | VS Code terminal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v4.5/green_pillar.py
Error     : Lane offset jumps by a full lane width
Terminal  : VS Code terminal
  $ python3 green_pillar.py
  offset: 0.02 -> 0.47 (one frame)
  lane lost for 0.3s
WHAT HAPPENED
  The lane offset jumped from center to a full lane width away in a single frame. The steering twitched violently and then recovered.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  When the line had a gap, the detector locked onto a neighboring line - the other lane's edge or a shadow - and reported it as the track line. The offset filter had no state, so one wrong frame was trusted completely for one control tick. Vision systems without temporal consistency treat every frame as a fresh truth, which amplifies single-frame errors.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by tracking the last-good line position and snapping back to it when the new detection is more than a lane-width away.

E0425 | v4.5 | SMALL | Found Day 71 | Fixed in 1 day | VS Code terminal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v4.5/green_pillar.py
Error     : Camera resolution mismatch with calibration
Terminal  : VS Code terminal
  $ python3 green_pillar.py
  cv2.error: (-215:Assertion failed)
  !src.empty() in function 'undistort'
WHAT HAPPENED
  The camera pipeline crashed on undistort. The calibration data loaded fine, so the mismatch was invisible until the function call.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The camera opened at 1280x720 but the calibration was done at 640x480. cv2.undistort requires the image size to match the camera matrix, and the mismatch triggered OpenCV's internal assertion. The two settings lived in different config files that were never cross-checked - one for the camera driver, one for the calibration loader.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by forcing both to the same resolution in camera_config.py and adding a boot check that compares the frame size with the calibration size.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
E0426 | v4.5 | SMALL | Found Day 71 | Fixed in 1 day | VS Code terminal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v4.5/green_pillar.py
Error     : HSV lower bound bigger than upper bound
Terminal  : VS Code terminal
  $ python3 green_pillar.py
  ValueError: lower should be smaller than upper
    File "green_pillar.py", line 34, in detect
WHAT HAPPENED
  The red pillar detector crashed the first time it processed a real frame. The color range that worked in tests was rejected by OpenCV.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  Red hue wraps around the HSV cylinder: red is both 0-10 and 170-180. Writing it as one continuous range (170..10) is invalid because lower > upper, which cv2.inRange rejects with a ValueError. The wrapper range is a conceptual mistake - the hue circle has no beginning, so the mask must be built from two disjoint ranges and OR-ed together.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by splitting the red range into two masks (0-10 and 170-180) and OR-ing the results, with a comment explaining the hue wrap.

E0432 | v4.5 | BIG | Found Day 72 | Fixed in 5 days | Pi SSH terminal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v4.5/green_pillar.py
Error     : Free space wrongly reports a corridor
Terminal  : Pi SSH terminal
  free space: 0.9m corridor detected
  reality: 0.4m gap
WHAT HAPPENED
  The free-space module reported a 0.9m corridor where only a 0.4m gap existed. The robot planned to drive through a space it could not fit through.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The fusion code averaged the ToF wall distance with the camera gap estimate. Averaging is only valid when both measurements describe the same quantity; here one sensor measured the wall and the other measured the gap, and the mean produced a number that matched neither reality. The 'corridor' was a pure artifact of mixing incompatible measurements.
INVESTIGATION (before the fix)
  - Reproduced the false corridor with the ToF and camera both active
  - Logged each sensor's raw value - they disagreed fundamentally
  - Tested taking the minimum instead of the mean - correct result
FIX (took 5 days)
  Fixed by taking the minimum of the two estimates (the conservative choice for a gap) and by storing the source of each free-space measurement.

Terminal  : Pi SSH terminal
  tracked: 10 frames, lost at frame 11
  pillar reappears 20 frames later
WHAT HAPPENED
  The tracker followed the pillar perfectly at low speed, then lost it the moment the robot accelerated. It always lost it at the same point on the approach.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The tracker searched a fixed window around the last known position. At 2m/s the pillar moves several pixels between frames, and once it left the search window the tracker had nothing to lock onto. The search window size was tuned for walking speed, not race speed. A tracker with no motion model is only as fast as its window is wide.
INVESTIGATION (before the fix)
  - Measured the pillar's inter-frame displacement at speed
  - Found the displacement exceeded the search window
  - Predicted the position with odometry - tracking held
FIX (took 5 days)
  Fixed by predicting the search window center with the odometry velocity before matching, and widening the window proportional to speed.

E0445 | v4.7 | SMALL | Found Day 75 | Fixed in 1 day | Pi console (HDMI)
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v4.7/pillar_dist.py
Error     : Corner detection misses 180-degree turns
Terminal  : Pi console (HDMI)
  $ python3 pillar_dist.py
  corner count = 0 after full lap
  expected 4 corners
WHAT HAPPENED
  The lap trace showed zero corners even though the robot clearly turned four times. The detector only watched distance, and the hairpin was too smooth.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The corner detector used a distance-only signature: it watched the wall distance change. A 180-degree turn made with a wide arc changes distance slowly and smoothly, so the slope never exceeded the trigger threshold. The signature was chosen for right-angle corners, and a different geometry produced a different signature entirely - one feature cannot describe all corner shapes.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by adding the heading-change signature from the IMU, and requiring both signatures for a confirmed corner.

E0446 | v4.7 | SMALL | Found Day 75 | Fixed in 1 day | Pi console (HDMI)
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v4.7/pillar_dist.py
Error     : Lane offset jumps by a full lane width
Terminal  : Pi console (HDMI)
  $ python3 pillar_dist.py
  offset: 0.02 -> 0.47 (one frame)
  lane lost for 0.3s
WHAT HAPPENED
  The lane offset jumped from center to a full lane width away in a single frame. The steering twitched violently and then recovered.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  When the line had a gap, the detector locked onto a neighboring line - the other lane's edge or a shadow - and reported it as the track line. The offset filter had no state, so one wrong frame was trusted completely for one control tick. Vision systems without temporal consistency treat every frame as a fresh truth, which amplifies single-frame errors.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by tracking the last-good line position and snapping back to it when the new detection is more than a lane-width away.

E0447 | v4.7 | SMALL | Found Day 75 | Fixed in 1 day | Pi console (HDMI)
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v4.7/pillar_dist.py
Error     : Camera resolution mismatch with calibration
Terminal  : Pi console (HDMI)
  $ python3 pillar_dist.py
  cv2.error: (-215:Assertion failed)
  !src.empty() in function 'undistort'
WHAT HAPPENED
  The camera pipeline crashed on undistort. The calibration data loaded fine, so the mismatch was invisible until the function call.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The camera opened at 1280x720 but the calibration was done at 640x480. cv2.undistort requires the image size to match the camera matrix, and the mismatch triggered OpenCV's internal assertion. The two settings lived in different config files that were never cross-checked - one for the camera driver, one for the calibration loader.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by forcing both to the same resolution in camera_config.py and adding a boot check that compares the frame size with the calibration size.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
E0448 | v4.7 | SMALL | Found Day 75 | Fixed in 1 day | Pi console (HDMI)
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v4.7/pillar_dist.py
Error     : HSV lower bound bigger than upper bound
Terminal  : Pi console (HDMI)
  $ python3 pillar_dist.py
  ValueError: lower should be smaller than upper
    File "pillar_dist.py", line 34, in detect
WHAT HAPPENED
  The red pillar detector crashed the first time it processed a real frame. The color range that worked in tests was rejected by OpenCV.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  Red hue wraps around the HSV cylinder: red is both 0-10 and 170-180. Writing it as one continuous range (170..10) is invalid because lower > upper, which cv2.inRange rejects with a ValueError. The wrapper range is a conceptual mistake - the hue circle has no beginning, so the mask must be built from two disjoint ranges and OR-ed together.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by splitting the red range into two masks (0-10 and 170-180) and OR-ing the results, with a comment explaining the hue wrap.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
E0449 | v4.7 | SMALL | Found Day 75 | Fixed in 1 day | Pi console (HDMI)
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v4.7/pillar_dist.py
Error     : ZeroDivisionError in distance estimate
Terminal  : Pi console (HDMI)
  $ python3 pillar_dist.py
    File "pillar_dist.py", line 58, in estimate
      dist = known_h / h
  ZeroDivisionError: float division by zero
WHAT HAPPENED
  The pillar distance estimator crashed mid-frame, not at startup. The contour had been found, but its height was zero.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The detector found a contour but the color filter had removed every interior pixel, leaving a height of zero. The distance formula assumes a valid height; dividing by zero raised ZeroDivisionError. This is a data-quality failure: the pipeline did not validate its input before applying the pinhole model, so a degenerate contour crashed the math instead of being skipped.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by skipping contours smaller than 5 pixels and returning 'unknown' instead of crashing when the height is invalid.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
E0450 | v4.7 | SMALL | Found Day 75 | Fixed in 1 day | Pi console (HDMI)
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v4.7/pillar_dist.py
Error     : Pillar detected at every frame edge
Terminal  : Pi console (HDMI)
  $ python3 pillar_dist.py
  pillar: (5, 20)  pillar: (610, 20)  ...
  false positives on the wall
WHAT HAPPENED
  The detector reported pillars at fixed screen positions in every frame. The track walls were being detected as red pillars.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The wall's edge pixels had similar HSV values to the pillar under the venue lighting, and the detector only matched color - it never checked size or shape. Any red-ish region, including a wall edge, passed the filter. A single-channel color test is necessary but not sufficient; without area and aspect-ratio constraints every similarly colored region is a candidate.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by adding a minimum area check and an aspect-ratio gate, and by masking the bottom 15% of the frame where the wall always appears.

E0451 | v4.7 | SMALL | Found Day 75 | Fixed in 1 day | Pi console (HDMI)
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v4.7/pillar_dist.py
Error     : Red and pink pillars are confused
Terminal  : Pi console (HDMI)
  $ python3 pillar_dist.py
  color=red  (was pink)
  confusion at hue 168-175
WHAT HAPPENED
  The color classifier called a pink pillar red. The two classes were defined by hue bands that overlapped, so the classification was ambiguous by construction.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  Pink and red differ in saturation and lightness, not much in hue. The classifier only used hue, so any pixel in the overlapping 168-175 band was claimed by both classes. Classifying colors by a single channel cannot separate classes that are distinct in a different channel - the feature space was too small for the problem.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by narrowing the red band and adding a saturation threshold of 90, since pink has measurably lower saturation than the official red.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
E0452 | v4.7 | SMALL | Found Day 75 | Fixed in 1 day | Pi console (HDMI)
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v4.7/pillar_dist.py
Error     : Free space is NaN after a corner
Terminal  : Pi console (HDMI)
  $ python3 pillar_dist.py
  free_space: nan
  corner left: nan
WHAT HAPPENED
  The free-space estimate became NaN at every corner. The robot continued driving, but the planner received garbage for the entire turn.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  While angling through a corner, the ToF reported 0mm (out of range), and the fusion code divided by that reading to normalize the estimate. NaN is infectious: one 0/0 poisons every downstream calculation, and because NaN comparisons are all false, no safety check could catch it. The corner is exactly where the sensor points at a gap, so this happened on every lap.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by replacing non-finite values with the sensor's max range and adding a validation pass that rejects NaN before fusion.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
E0453 | v4.7 | BIG | Found Day 76 | Fixed in 2 days | Pi SSH terminal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v4.7/pillar_dist.py
Error     : Green pillar invisible on the grass backdrop
Terminal  : Pi SSH terminal
  green pillar: 0 pixels
  backdrop hue matches the pillar
WHAT HAPPENED
  The green pillar detector found zero pixels while the pillar sat in plain view. The practice field behind it was green too.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The green pillar and the green grass shared the same hue range, so the color filter selected the entire background and the detector's foreground logic found nothing - the pillar was invisible because the background was identical. Color is not a sufficient feature when the background shares the color; the detector needed a feature the backdrop lacks, such as the pillar's frame edges.
INVESTIGATION (before the fix)
  - Sampled the pillar and grass hues - nearly identical
  - Tested the detector against a neutral background - worked
  - Confirmed the failure was contrast, not calibration
FIX (took 2 days)
  Fixed by detecting the red frame around the pillar as the primary signature, and using the green fill only as confirmation.

E0454 | v4.7 | BIG | Found Day 76 | Fixed in 3 days | Pi SSH terminal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v4.7/pillar_dist.py
Error     : Free space wrongly reports a corridor
Terminal  : Pi SSH terminal
  free space: 0.9m corridor detected
  reality: 0.4m gap
WHAT HAPPENED
  The free-space module reported a 0.9m corridor where only a 0.4m gap existed. The robot planned to drive through a space it could not fit through.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The fusion code averaged the ToF wall distance with the camera gap estimate. Averaging is only valid when both measurements describe the same quantity; here one sensor measured the wall and the other measured the gap, and the mean produced a number that matched neither reality. The 'corridor' was a pure artifact of mixing incompatible measurements.
INVESTIGATION (before the fix)
  - Reproduced the false corridor with the ToF and camera both active
  - Logged each sensor's raw value - they disagreed fundamentally
  - Tested taking the minimum instead of the mean - correct result
FIX (took 3 days)
  Fixed by taking the minimum of the two estimates (the conservative choice for a gap) and by storing the source of each free-space measurement.

E0456 | v4.7 | BIG | Found Day 76 | Fixed in 5 days | Pi SSH terminal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v4.7/pillar_dist.py
Error     : Pillar never detected under venue lights
Terminal  : Pi SSH terminal
  pillars: 0 found (12 frames)
  HSV test on the phone: 0 found
  color bands all wrong
WHAT HAPPENED
  The pillar detector found nothing for the entire morning. The same code had detected pillars perfectly in the lab the day before.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The morning sun changed the color temperature of the light, shifting every color's HSV values. Fixed HSV bands are calibrated for one lighting condition; a different light source moves the same physical color to a different point in HSV space. Vision systems are lighting-dependent by nature - the color of light is part of the measurement, not a nuisance term.
INVESTIGATION (before the fix)
  - Confirmed detection worked in the lab under fluorescent light
  - Sampled the pillar's HSV values under the morning sun
  - Compared the sampled values with the configured bands
FIX (took 5 days)
  Fixed by re-running the color calibration on the venue floor at the same time of day as the competition, and by making the calibration tool part of the morning routine.

E0468 | v4.8 | BIG | Found Day 78 | Fixed in 5 days | Pi SSH terminal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v4.8/track_pillars.py
Error     : Visual odometry scale explodes after a turn
Terminal  : Pi SSH terminal
  vo scale: 1.0 -> 9.3
  pose jumps 0.4m per frame
WHAT HAPPENED
  After the 90-degree turn, the visual odometry started reporting absurd distances - the pose jumped 0.4 meters per frame while the robot moved a few centimeters.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  Visual odometry estimates motion from feature point displacement and derives the scale from the baseline between frames. After a sharp turn, feature matching lost the reference set and re-matched against a new baseline, and the scale estimate - unconstrained by any absolute reference - diverged. Monocular scale is only observable while the same features persist; a turn breaks that chain.
INVESTIGATION (before the fix)
  - Plotted the scale factor over time - flat before the turn, exploding after
  - Counted matched features across the turn - dropped below the threshold
  - Replayed the turn with forced re-initialization - problem vanished
FIX (took 5 days)
  Fixed by re-initializing the baseline when the matched feature count drops below 20, and by clamping the scale factor to a physically plausible range.

  The color classifier called a pink pillar red. The two classes were defined by hue bands that overlapped, so the classification was ambiguous by construction.

Terminal  : Windows CMD
  $ python3 visual_odometry.py
  free_space: nan

WHAT HAPPENED
  The free-space estimate became NaN at every corner. The robot continued driving, but the planner received garbage for the entire turn.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)

WHAT HAPPENED
  The tracker followed the pillar perfectly at low speed, then lost it the moment the robot accelerated. It always lost it at the same point on the approach.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)

  - Predicted the position with odometry - tracking held

E0479 | v4.9 | BIG | Found Day 80 | Fixed in 4 days | Pi SSH terminal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v4.9/benchmark_vo.py
Error     : Visual odometry scale explodes after a turn
Terminal  : Pi SSH terminal
  vo scale: 1.0 -> 9.3
  pose jumps 0.4m per frame
WHAT HAPPENED
  After the 90-degree turn, the visual odometry started reporting absurd distances - the pose jumped 0.4 meters per frame while the robot moved a few centimeters.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  Visual odometry estimates motion from feature point displacement and derives the scale from the baseline between frames. After a sharp turn, feature matching lost the reference set and re-matched against a new baseline, and the scale estimate - unconstrained by any absolute reference - diverged. Monocular scale is only observable while the same features persist; a turn breaks that chain.
INVESTIGATION (before the fix)
  - Plotted the scale factor over time - flat before the turn, exploding after
  - Counted matched features across the turn - dropped below the threshold
  - Replayed the turn with forced re-initialization - problem vanished
FIX (took 4 days)
  Fixed by re-initializing the baseline when the matched feature count drops below 20, and by clamping the scale factor to a physically plausible range.

E0481 | v5.0 | SMALL | Found Day 81 | Fixed in 1 day | systemd journal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v5.0/dead_reckon.py
Error     : np.linalg.LinAlgError: Singular matrix
Terminal  : systemd journal
  $ python3 dead_reckon.py
    File "dead_reckon.py", line 92, in update
      K = P @ H @ inv(S)
  np.linalg.LinAlgError: Singular matrix
WHAT HAPPENED
  The UKF crashed on its first update with all sensors dead. The innovation covariance was singular - the filter had no information at all.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  With every sensor returning zero, the innovation covariance S became singular (determinant zero), and matrix inversion is undefined for singular matrices. The UKF assumes measurements carry some information; all-zero measurements violate that assumption. Mathematically this is the filter asking for the inverse of a zero matrix - the error is the correct behavior of the math, and the bug is that nothing prevented it.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by checking the condition number of S before the update and skipping the update when it exceeds a threshold, keeping the prediction only.

E0482 | v5.0 | SMALL | Found Day 81 | Fixed in 1 day | systemd journal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v5.0/motion_tracker.py
Error     : NaN appears in the covariance matrix
Terminal  : systemd journal
  $ python3 motion_tracker.py
  P = [[nan nan],[nan nan]]
  pose estimate frozen
WHAT HAPPENED
  The covariance matrix filled with NaN and the pose stopped updating. The filter neither crashed nor recovered - it just froze.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  One corrupted measurement (a 0 divided during normalization) introduced NaN into the state, and every subsequent update propagated it through the linear algebra. The UKF has no built-in NaN detection; NaN arithmetic silently poisons every matrix product. The failure showed up minutes later as a frozen pose, long after the bad sample was long gone.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by validating every measurement with np.isfinite() before the update and rejecting non-finite samples with a logged warning.

E0483 | v5.0 | SMALL | Found Day 81 | Fixed in 1 day | systemd journal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v5.0/dead_reckon.py
Error     : Negative variance in the dead reckoning
Terminal  : systemd journal
  $ python3 dead_reckon.py
  variance: -0.004
  sigma = nan
WHAT HAPPENED
  The dead-reckoning output contained a negative variance, and the standard deviation computed from it became NaN. The motion estimate was mathematically impossible.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The noise model added a negative correction term after a wheel-slip event - slip reduces the estimated speed, and the speed-dependent noise formula produced a negative variance. Variance is defined as the expected squared deviation, which cannot be negative; the formula was wrong for the slip regime. Negative variance then breaks the sqrt used for the 1-sigma bound.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by clamping the variance to a minimum of 1e-6 and adding an assertion in tests that the variance never leaves the valid domain.

E0484 | v5.0 | SMALL | Found Day 81 | Fixed in 1 day | systemd journal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v5.0/motion_tracker.py
Error     : Outlier rejection drops 100% of measurements
Terminal  : systemd journal
  $ python3 motion_tracker.py
  accepted: 0/48 measurements
  pose drifts with no updates
WHAT HAPPENED
  The filter never updated - every single measurement was rejected as an outlier. The robot moved, but the pose estimate just drifted open-loop.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The Mahalanobis gate used chi-square threshold 3 (about 1 sigma) for a measurement that legitimately carries 2-3 sigma noise. With the gate set tighter than the noise, every genuine reading exceeded the threshold and was discarded. Outlier rejection assumes the model matches the noise; a gate calibrated for a different sensor or surface rejects the true signal as noise.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by raising the gate to chi-square 9 (3 sigma), then validating with the outlier_test that at least 95% of genuine measurements pass.

E0485 | v5.0 | SMALL | Found Day 81 | Fixed in 1 day | systemd journal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v5.0/dead_reckon.py
Error     : UKF alpha/beta/kappa parameter typo
Terminal  : systemd journal
  $ python3 dead_reckon.py
  ukf_params.json: alpha=1e-3 beta=2 kappa=1
  filter diverges on the first turn
WHAT HAPPENED
  The UKF diverged instantly on the first corner. The same data worked with the old parameters, so the filter itself was fine - the tuning was not.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The sigma-point spread parameter alpha controls how far the sigma points lie from the mean. alpha=1e-3 collapsed the sigma points almost onto the mean, so the filter's covariance estimate was tiny and it over-trusted its state. On the first turn the innovation was huge relative to that shrunken covariance, and the correction pulled the state wildly off. One digit in a JSON file changed the filter's behavior completely.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by restoring alpha=1e-2 from the tuning run and adding a startup check that alpha is within the valid (0,1] range.

E0486 | v5.0 | SMALL | Found Day 81 | Fixed in 1 day | systemd journal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v5.0/motion_tracker.py
Error     : Mag heading jumps 180 degrees on reversal
Terminal  : systemd journal
  $ python3 motion_tracker.py
  heading: 45 -> 225 (robot didn't turn)
  hard-iron offset missing
WHAT HAPPENED
  The heading readout flipped by exactly 180 degrees whenever the robot reversed direction. The robot never turned, but the compass said it had.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The hard-iron offset (the fixed magnetic distortion from the battery and wiring) was only applied in forward direction code paths. When reversing, the un-compensated raw vector rotated the heading by the offset magnitude - which here was almost exactly 180 degrees. The magnetometer measures the sum of the Earth field plus the constant distortion; without subtracting the distortion the heading formula is wrong.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by applying the calibrated hard-iron offset in both directions and adding the reverse path to the heading test cases.

E0487 | v5.0 | SMALL | Found Day 81 | Fixed in 1 day | systemd journal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v5.0/dead_reckon.py
Error     : Cross-verify reports 40cm disagreement
Terminal  : systemd journal
  $ python3 dead_reckon.py
  tof=0.82m  camera=0.42m  diff=0.40m
  camera scale wrong
WHAT HAPPENED
  The ToF and camera distance estimates disagreed by 40cm on the same target. One of them was right; the cross-verify test existed precisely to find which.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The camera distance scale was calibrated at 640x480, but the pipeline ran at 1280x720. The focal length in pixels doubles with resolution, so a scale factor valid at one resolution is wrong at the other. The two systems measured correctly in their own frames - the bug was a unit mismatch between the calibration domain and the runtime domain.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by re-running tof_camera_calib.py at the runtime resolution and storing the resolution in the calibration file so the scale can be validated at load.
