E0488 | v5.0 | SMALL | Found Day 81 | Fixed in 1 day | systemd journal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v5.0/motion_tracker.py
Error     : EKF linearization fails on sharp turns
Terminal  : systemd journal
  $ python3 motion_tracker.py
  ekf error: Jacobian is zero
  state: x=0.5 y=2.1 theta=nan
WHAT HAPPENED
  The EKF produced NaN heading on sharp turns. The filter worked on gentle curves and fell apart on the aggressive ones.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The EKF linearizes the motion model with a Jacobian evaluated at the current state. For a sharp turn the yaw Jacobian term was dropped in the model, so the Jacobian row became zero and the state transition lost its heading information - the estimate collapsed to NaN. The EKF's approximation quality depends on the Jacobian being accurate; a model simplified for straight driving is invalid at large steering angles.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by adding the missing yaw-dynamics term to the Jacobian and extending the ekf_test with a sharp-turn scenario.

E0489 | v5.0 | BIG | Found Day 82 | Fixed in 2 days | Pi SSH terminal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v5.0/dead_reckon.py
Error     : UKF diverges and the robot drives off the track
Terminal  : Pi SSH terminal
  ukf: x=3.2 y=8.9 theta=2.1
  actual: x=1.8 y=2.0 theta=0.0
  UKF diverged, EKF fallback used
WHAT HAPPENED
  The robot drove off the track because the UKF believed the robot was somewhere else entirely. The pose was confident, detailed - and completely wrong.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The adaptive noise module grew the process noise with each suspicious measurement, and the filter's confidence in the state shrank with it. With enough noise inflation the filter trusted every new measurement blindly, and a single bad sensor reading dragged the pose far from reality. The adaptive mechanism had no upper bound on the noise it would tolerate - it adapted itself into failure.
INVESTIGATION (before the fix)
  - Plotted the UKF pose against the known track - divergence was gradual
  - Tracked the process noise growth over the run
  - Bounded the noise growth and re-ran - divergence gone
FIX (took 2 days)
  Fixed by bounding the adaptive noise growth to a maximum factor, and by adding a sanity gate that falls back to the EKF when the UKF and EKF disagree by more than 1m.

E0490 | v5.0 | BIG | Found Day 82 | Fixed in 3 days | Pi SSH terminal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v5.0/motion_tracker.py
Error     : Dead reckoning drifts 30cm per lap
Terminal  : Pi SSH terminal
  dead reckoning: -0.30m off after 1 lap
  wheel slip on the carpet
WHAT HAPPENED
  The dead-reckoned position was 30cm off after every lap. The error was consistent, which made it diagnosable - and unavoidable without external reference.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  Odometry assumes the wheels roll without slipping, but the carpet caused a consistent 3% slip that odometry cannot measure - it only counts rotations. Over a 10m lap, 3% is exactly 30cm. Pure dead reckoning has no way to know about slip because the encoder counts the same whether the wheel grips or slides; the model was perfect, the assumption was wrong.
INVESTIGATION (before the fix)
  - Measured the error over several laps - constant at 30cm
  - Computed the implied slip percentage - 3%, consistent
  - Fused the ToF wall distance as a lateral reference
FIX (took 3 days)
  Fixed by fusing the ToF wall distance into the lateral state, so the drift is corrected by an absolute reference instead of a second integration.

E0491 | v5.0 | BIG | Found Day 82 | Fixed in 4 days | Pi SSH terminal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v5.0/dead_reckon.py
Error     : EKF position jumps 40cm at the first corner
Terminal  : Pi SSH terminal
  position: (1.2, 2.0) -> (1.6, 2.0) in one step
  measurement noise too small
WHAT HAPPENED
  At the first corner the EKF position jumped 40cm in a single update. The jump was instant - the filter re-trusted a single measurement over its own model.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The measurement noise matrix was tuned too optimistically: the filter believed the ToF more than the motion model. At the corner, one noisy reading passed the gate and the filter snapped to it. The EKF's estimate is a weighted compromise; the weights live in the noise matrices, so a too-small R matrix means 'trust the sensor blindly'.
INVESTIGATION (before the fix)
  - Logged the innovation at the corner - it was 10x the modeled noise
  - Tuned R against real logged data instead of guesses
  - Verified the jump disappeared with the realistic R
FIX (took 4 days)
  Fixed by tuning the measurement noise matrix from actual logged data (Allan variance for the sensors), and by gating the correction when the innovation exceeds 5 sigma.

E0492 | v5.0 | BIG | Found Day 82 | Fixed in 5 days | Pi SSH terminal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v5.0/motion_tracker.py
Error     : Pose pipeline slows to 8Hz under load
Terminal  : Pi SSH terminal
  pipeline rate: 100Hz -> 8Hz
  CPU at 96% (vision + fusion)
WHAT HAPPENED
  The pose pipeline collapsed from 100Hz to 8Hz when the vision stack ran at full load. The robot's control degraded with it, because control depends on fresh pose data.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  Vision and fusion ran in a single thread, and vision processing took 120ms per frame under load. The GIL serialized the Python work, so fusion starved behind vision. The architecture had no isolation between a 30fps vision workload and a 100Hz fusion workload - one process, one thread, one bottleneck.
INVESTIGATION (before the fix)
  - Measured the per-stage latency to find the bottleneck
  - Confirmed vision occupied the CPU while fusion waited
  - Split fusion into a separate process - rate recovered
FIX (took 5 days)
  Fixed by moving fusion to its own process with a shared-memory pose buffer, so a vision slowdown can no longer block control.

  Fixed by adding the missing yaw-dynamics term to the Jacobian and extending the ekf_test with a sharp-turn scenario.

E0500 | v5.1 | SMALL | Found Day 83 | Fixed in 1 day | VS Code terminal

File      : history/v5.1/motor_interference_test.py
Error     : np.linalg.LinAlgError: Singular matrix
Terminal  : VS Code terminal

    File "motor_interference_test.py", line 92, in update
      K = P @ H @ inv(S)

  The UKF crashed on its first update with all sensors dead. The innovation covariance was singular - the filter had no information at all.

E0501 | v5.1 | BIG | Found Day 84 | Fixed in 2 days | Pi SSH terminal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v5.1/mag_heading.py
Error     : Dead reckoning drifts 30cm per lap
Terminal  : Pi SSH terminal
  dead reckoning: -0.30m off after 1 lap
  wheel slip on the carpet
WHAT HAPPENED
  The dead-reckoned position was 30cm off after every lap. The error was consistent, which made it diagnosable - and unavoidable without external reference.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  Odometry assumes the wheels roll without slipping, but the carpet caused a consistent 3% slip that odometry cannot measure - it only counts rotations. Over a 10m lap, 3% is exactly 30cm. Pure dead reckoning has no way to know about slip because the encoder counts the same whether the wheel grips or slides; the model was perfect, the assumption was wrong.
INVESTIGATION (before the fix)
  - Measured the error over several laps - constant at 30cm
  - Computed the implied slip percentage - 3%, consistent
  - Fused the ToF wall distance as a lateral reference
FIX (took 2 days)
  Fixed by fusing the ToF wall distance into the lateral state, so the drift is corrected by an absolute reference instead of a second integration.

E0502 | v5.1 | BIG | Found Day 84 | Fixed in 3 days | Pi SSH terminal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v5.1/motor_interference_test.py
Error     : EKF position jumps 40cm at the first corner
Terminal  : Pi SSH terminal
  position: (1.2, 2.0) -> (1.6, 2.0) in one step
  measurement noise too small
WHAT HAPPENED
  At the first corner the EKF position jumped 40cm in a single update. The jump was instant - the filter re-trusted a single measurement over its own model.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The measurement noise matrix was tuned too optimistically: the filter believed the ToF more than the motion model. At the corner, one noisy reading passed the gate and the filter snapped to it. The EKF's estimate is a weighted compromise; the weights live in the noise matrices, so a too-small R matrix means 'trust the sensor blindly'.
INVESTIGATION (before the fix)
  - Logged the innovation at the corner - it was 10x the modeled noise
  - Tuned R against real logged data instead of guesses
  - Verified the jump disappeared with the realistic R
FIX (took 3 days)
  Fixed by tuning the measurement noise matrix from actual logged data (Allan variance for the sensors), and by gating the correction when the innovation exceeds 5 sigma.

E0503 | v5.1 | BIG | Found Day 84 | Fixed in 4 days | Pi SSH terminal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v5.1/mag_heading.py
Error     : Pose pipeline slows to 8Hz under load
Terminal  : Pi SSH terminal
  pipeline rate: 100Hz -> 8Hz
  CPU at 96% (vision + fusion)
WHAT HAPPENED
  The pose pipeline collapsed from 100Hz to 8Hz when the vision stack ran at full load. The robot's control degraded with it, because control depends on fresh pose data.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  Vision and fusion ran in a single thread, and vision processing took 120ms per frame under load. The GIL serialized the Python work, so fusion starved behind vision. The architecture had no isolation between a 30fps vision workload and a 100Hz fusion workload - one process, one thread, one bottleneck.
INVESTIGATION (before the fix)
  - Measured the per-stage latency to find the bottleneck
  - Confirmed vision occupied the CPU while fusion waited
  - Split fusion into a separate process - rate recovered
FIX (took 4 days)
  Fixed by moving fusion to its own process with a shared-memory pose buffer, so a vision slowdown can no longer block control.

E0504 | v5.1 | BIG | Found Day 84 | Fixed in 5 days | Pi SSH terminal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v5.1/motor_interference_test.py
Error     : Outlier rejection masks a real obstacle
Terminal  : Pi SSH terminal
  obstacle at 0.5m: REJECTED as outlier
  robot drives into the pillar
WHAT HAPPENED
  The outlier filter rejected the most important reading of the day: the real pillar at 0.5m. The robot drove into the obstacle it was supposed to avoid.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The Mahalanobis gate was tuned against a history of far-field noise, so the first close-range reading looked statistically impossible - it was far outside the modeled distribution. Outlier rejection assumes outliers are errors, but here the outlier was the truth and the history was the error. No static gate can distinguish 'new truth' from 'garbage' by distance alone.
INVESTIGATION (before the fix)
  - Replayed the log - the 0.5m reading was the true pillar
  - Checked the gate: the reading was rejected as 8-sigma
  - Tested an asymmetric gate - near readings never rejected
FIX (took 5 days)
  Fixed by making the gate asymmetric: readings below 0.6m are always accepted (they can only be obstacles), and only far-field readings are subject to rejection.

E0505 | v5.2 | SMALL | Found Day 85 | Fixed in 1 day | Pi SSH terminal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v5.2/attitude_test.py
Error     : Negative variance in the dead reckoning
Terminal  : Pi SSH terminal
  $ python3 attitude_test.py
  variance: -0.004
  sigma = nan
WHAT HAPPENED
  The dead-reckoning output contained a negative variance, and the standard deviation computed from it became NaN. The motion estimate was mathematically impossible.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The noise model added a negative correction term after a wheel-slip event - slip reduces the estimated speed, and the speed-dependent noise formula produced a negative variance. Variance is defined as the expected squared deviation, which cannot be negative; the formula was wrong for the slip regime. Negative variance then breaks the sqrt used for the 1-sigma bound.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by clamping the variance to a minimum of 1e-6 and adding an assertion in tests that the variance never leaves the valid domain.

E0506 | v5.2 | SMALL | Found Day 85 | Fixed in 1 day | Pi SSH terminal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v5.2/complementary_full.py
Error     : Outlier rejection drops 100% of measurements
Terminal  : Pi SSH terminal
  $ python3 complementary_full.py
  accepted: 0/48 measurements
  pose drifts with no updates
WHAT HAPPENED
  The filter never updated - every single measurement was rejected as an outlier. The robot moved, but the pose estimate just drifted open-loop.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The Mahalanobis gate used chi-square threshold 3 (about 1 sigma) for a measurement that legitimately carries 2-3 sigma noise. With the gate set tighter than the noise, every genuine reading exceeded the threshold and was discarded. Outlier rejection assumes the model matches the noise; a gate calibrated for a different sensor or surface rejects the true signal as noise.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by raising the gate to chi-square 9 (3 sigma), then validating with the outlier_test that at least 95% of genuine measurements pass.

E0507 | v5.2 | SMALL | Found Day 85 | Fixed in 1 day | Pi SSH terminal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v5.2/attitude_test.py
Error     : UKF alpha/beta/kappa parameter typo
Terminal  : Pi SSH terminal
  $ python3 attitude_test.py
  ukf_params.json: alpha=1e-3 beta=2 kappa=1
  filter diverges on the first turn
WHAT HAPPENED
  The UKF diverged instantly on the first corner. The same data worked with the old parameters, so the filter itself was fine - the tuning was not.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The sigma-point spread parameter alpha controls how far the sigma points lie from the mean. alpha=1e-3 collapsed the sigma points almost onto the mean, so the filter's covariance estimate was tiny and it over-trusted its state. On the first turn the innovation was huge relative to that shrunken covariance, and the correction pulled the state wildly off. One digit in a JSON file changed the filter's behavior completely.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by restoring alpha=1e-2 from the tuning run and adding a startup check that alpha is within the valid (0,1] range.

E0508 | v5.2 | SMALL | Found Day 85 | Fixed in 1 day | Pi SSH terminal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v5.2/complementary_full.py
Error     : Mag heading jumps 180 degrees on reversal
Terminal  : Pi SSH terminal
  $ python3 complementary_full.py
  heading: 45 -> 225 (robot didn't turn)
  hard-iron offset missing
WHAT HAPPENED
  The heading readout flipped by exactly 180 degrees whenever the robot reversed direction. The robot never turned, but the compass said it had.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The hard-iron offset (the fixed magnetic distortion from the battery and wiring) was only applied in forward direction code paths. When reversing, the un-compensated raw vector rotated the heading by the offset magnitude - which here was almost exactly 180 degrees. The magnetometer measures the sum of the Earth field plus the constant distortion; without subtracting the distortion the heading formula is wrong.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by applying the calibrated hard-iron offset in both directions and adding the reverse path to the heading test cases.

E0509 | v5.2 | SMALL | Found Day 85 | Fixed in 1 day | Pi SSH terminal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v5.2/attitude_test.py
Error     : Cross-verify reports 40cm disagreement
Terminal  : Pi SSH terminal
  $ python3 attitude_test.py
  tof=0.82m  camera=0.42m  diff=0.40m
  camera scale wrong
WHAT HAPPENED
  The ToF and camera distance estimates disagreed by 40cm on the same target. One of them was right; the cross-verify test existed precisely to find which.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The camera distance scale was calibrated at 640x480, but the pipeline ran at 1280x720. The focal length in pixels doubles with resolution, so a scale factor valid at one resolution is wrong at the other. The two systems measured correctly in their own frames - the bug was a unit mismatch between the calibration domain and the runtime domain.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by re-running tof_camera_calib.py at the runtime resolution and storing the resolution in the calibration file so the scale can be validated at load.

E0510 | v5.2 | SMALL | Found Day 85 | Fixed in 1 day | Pi SSH terminal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v5.2/complementary_full.py
Error     : EKF linearization fails on sharp turns
Terminal  : Pi SSH terminal
  $ python3 complementary_full.py
  ekf error: Jacobian is zero
  state: x=0.5 y=2.1 theta=nan
WHAT HAPPENED
  The EKF produced NaN heading on sharp turns. The filter worked on gentle curves and fell apart on the aggressive ones.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The EKF linearizes the motion model with a Jacobian evaluated at the current state. For a sharp turn the yaw Jacobian term was dropped in the model, so the Jacobian row became zero and the state transition lost its heading information - the estimate collapsed to NaN. The EKF's approximation quality depends on the Jacobian being accurate; a model simplified for straight driving is invalid at large steering angles.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by adding the missing yaw-dynamics term to the Jacobian and extending the ekf_test with a sharp-turn scenario.

E0512 | v5.2 | SMALL | Found Day 85 | Fixed in 1 day | Pi SSH terminal

Error     : NaN appears in the covariance matrix
Terminal  : Pi SSH terminal

  pose estimate frozen
WHAT HAPPENED
  The covariance matrix filled with NaN and the pose stopped updating. The filter neither crashed nor recovered - it just froze.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  One corrupted measurement (a 0 divided during normalization) introduced NaN into the state, and every subsequent update propagated it through the linear algebra. Outlier rejection assumes outliers are errors, but here the outlier was the truth and the history was the error. No static gate can distinguish 'new truth' from 'garbage' by distance alone.
INVESTIGATION (before the fix)
  - Replayed the log - the 0.5m reading was the true pillar
  - Checked the gate: the reading was rejected as 8-sigma
  - Tested an asymmetric gate - near readings never rejected
FIX (took 3 days)
  Fixed by making the gate asymmetric: readings below 0.6m are always accepted (they can only be obstacles), and only far-field readings are subject to rejection.

E0527 | v5.3 | BIG | Found Day 88 | Fixed in 4 days | Pi SSH terminal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v5.3/ekf_localization.py
Error     : Cross-verify fails after sensor warm-up
Terminal  : Pi SSH terminal
  tof=0.81m camera=0.30m diff=0.51m
  sensor mismatch after 10 minutes
WHAT HAPPENED
  The ToF and camera agreed for the first ten minutes, then diverged by half a meter. The cross-verify check that catches drift was the thing that drifted.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The ToF's range output shifts with temperature as the laser diode's characteristics change, and after 10 minutes of operation the module had warmed several degrees.   - Correlated the drift with temperature - a linear fit explained it
FIX (took 4 days)
  Fixed by adding a temperature correction computed from the linear fit, applied to the ToF readings in the fusion layer.

E0528 | v5.3 | BIG | Found Day 88 | Fixed in 5 days | Pi SSH terminal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v5.3/ekf_test.py
Error     : Attitude flips 180 degrees during fast yaw
Terminal  : Pi SSH terminal
  roll: 0 -> 180 (fast yaw)
  gimbal lock in Euler representation
WHAT HAPPENED
  During a fast turn the reported roll flipped from 0 to 180 degrees. The robot never rolled at all - the representation of the attitude broke, not the robot.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The attitude was stored as Euler angles (roll, pitch, yaw). Euler angles suffer gimbal lock: when the pitch approaches 90 degrees, roll and yaw become the same axis and the representation degenerates, producing 180-degree jumps. The physical attitude was continuous; the Euler representation made it discontinuous. This is a mathematical property of the representation, not a sensor or filter bug.
INVESTIGATION (before the fix)
  - Replayed the attitude - the flip coincided exactly with the yaw peak
  - Tested the same motion in simulation - the flip reproduced
  - Switched to quaternion storage - the flip vanished
FIX (took 5 days)
  Fixed by switching the attitude storage to quaternions, converting to Euler only for display, and adding a unit-quaternion normalization after every update.

E0529 | v5.4 | SMALL | Found Day 89 | Fixed in 1 day | ESP32 serial monitor
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v5.4/ukf_localization.py
Error     : UKF alpha/beta/kappa parameter typo
Terminal  : ESP32 serial monitor
  $ python3 ukf_localization.py
  ukf_params.json: alpha=1e-3 beta=2 kappa=1
  filter diverges on the first turn
WHAT HAPPENED
  The UKF diverged instantly on the first corner. The same data worked with the old parameters, so the filter itself was fine - the tuning was not.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The sigma-point spread parameter alpha controls how far the sigma points lie from the mean. alpha=1e-3 collapsed the sigma points almost onto the mean, so the filter's covariance estimate was tiny and it over-trusted its state. On the first turn the innovation was huge relative to that shrunken covariance, and the correction pulled the state wildly off. One digit in a JSON file changed the filter's behavior completely.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by restoring alpha=1e-2 from the tuning run and adding a startup check that alpha is within the valid (0,1] range.

E0530 | v5.4 | SMALL | Found Day 89 | Fixed in 1 day | ESP32 serial monitor
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v5.4/ukf_vs_ekf.py
Error     : Mag heading jumps 180 degrees on reversal
Terminal  : ESP32 serial monitor
  $ python3 ukf_vs_ekf.py
  heading: 45 -> 225 (robot didn't turn)
  hard-iron offset missing
WHAT HAPPENED
  The heading readout flipped by exactly 180 degrees whenever the robot reversed direction. The robot never turned, but the compass said it had.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The hard-iron offset (the fixed magnetic distortion from the battery and wiring) was only applied in forward direction code paths. When reversing, the un-compensated raw vector rotated the heading by the offset magnitude - which here was almost exactly 180 degrees. The magnetometer measures the sum of the Earth field plus the constant distortion; without subtracting the distortion the heading formula is wrong.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by applying the calibrated hard-iron offset in both directions and adding the reverse path to the heading test cases.

E0531 | v5.4 | SMALL | Found Day 89 | Fixed in 1 day | ESP32 serial monitor
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v5.4/ukf_localization.py
Error     : Cross-verify reports 40cm disagreement
Terminal  : ESP32 serial monitor
  $ python3 ukf_localization.py
  tof=0.82m  camera=0.42m  diff=0.40m
  camera scale wrong
WHAT HAPPENED
  The ToF and camera distance estimates disagreed by 40cm on the same target. One of them was right; the cross-verify test existed precisely to find which.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The camera distance scale was calibrated at 640x480, but the pipeline ran at 1280x720. The focal length in pixels doubles with resolution, so a scale factor valid at one resolution is wrong at the other. The two systems measured correctly in their own frames - the bug was a unit mismatch between the calibration domain and the runtime domain.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by re-running tof_camera_calib.py at the runtime resolution and storing the resolution in the calibration file so the scale can be validated at load.

E0532 | v5.4 | SMALL | Found Day 89 | Fixed in 1 day | ESP32 serial monitor
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v5.4/ukf_vs_ekf.py
Error     : EKF linearization fails on sharp turns
Terminal  : ESP32 serial monitor
  $ python3 ukf_vs_ekf.py
  ekf error: Jacobian is zero
  state: x=0.5 y=2.1 theta=nan
WHAT HAPPENED
  The EKF produced NaN heading on sharp turns. The filter worked on gentle curves and fell apart on the aggressive ones.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The EKF linearizes the motion model with a Jacobian evaluated at the current state. For a sharp turn the yaw Jacobian term was dropped in the model, so the Jacobian row became zero and the state transition lost its heading information - the estimate collapsed to NaN. The EKF's approximation quality depends on the Jacobian being accurate; a model simplified for straight driving is invalid at large steering angles.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by adding the missing yaw-dynamics term to the Jacobian and extending the ekf_test with a sharp-turn scenario.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
E0533 | v5.4 | SMALL | Found Day 89 | Fixed in 1 day | ESP32 serial monitor
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v5.4/ukf_localization.py
Error     : np.linalg.LinAlgError: Singular matrix
Terminal  : ESP32 serial monitor
  $ python3 ukf_localization.py
    File "ukf_localization.py", line 92, in update
      K = P @ H @ inv(S)
  np.linalg.LinAlgError: Singular matrix
WHAT HAPPENED
  The UKF crashed on its first update with all sensors dead. The innovation covariance was singular - the filter had no information at all.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  With every sensor returning zero, the innovation covariance S became singular (determinant zero), and matrix inversion is undefined for singular matrices. The UKF assumes measurements carry some information; all-zero measurements violate that assumption. Mathematically this is the filter asking for the inverse of a zero matrix - the error is the correct behavior of the math, and the bug is that nothing prevented it.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by checking the condition number of S before the update and skipping the update when it exceeds a threshold, keeping the prediction only.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
E0534 | v5.4 | SMALL | Found Day 89 | Fixed in 1 day | ESP32 serial monitor
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v5.4/ukf_vs_ekf.py
Error     : NaN appears in the covariance matrix
Terminal  : ESP32 serial monitor
  $ python3 ukf_vs_ekf.py
  P = [[nan nan],[nan nan]]
  pose estimate frozen
WHAT HAPPENED
  The covariance matrix filled with NaN and the pose stopped updating. The filter neither crashed nor recovered - it just froze.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  One corrupted measurement (a 0 divided during normalization) introduced NaN into the state, and every subsequent update propagated it through the linear algebra. The UKF has no built-in NaN detection; NaN arithmetic silently poisons every matrix product. The failure showed up minutes later as a frozen pose, long after the bad sample was long gone.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by validating every measurement with np.isfinite() before the update and rejecting non-finite samples with a logged warning.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
E0535 | v5.4 | SMALL | Found Day 89 | Fixed in 1 day | ESP32 serial monitor
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v5.4/ukf_localization.py
Error     : Negative variance in the dead reckoning
Terminal  : ESP32 serial monitor
  $ python3 ukf_localization.py
  variance: -0.004
  sigma = nan
WHAT HAPPENED
  The dead-reckoning output contained a negative variance, and the standard deviation computed from it became NaN. The motion estimate was mathematically impossible.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The noise model added a negative correction term after a wheel-slip event - slip reduces the estimated speed, and the speed-dependent noise formula produced a negative variance. Variance is defined as the expected squared deviation, which cannot be negative; the formula was wrong for the slip regime. Negative variance then breaks the sqrt used for the 1-sigma bound.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by clamping the variance to a minimum of 1e-6 and adding an assertion in tests that the variance never leaves the valid domain.

E0536 | v5.4 | SMALL | Found Day 89 | Fixed in 1 day | ESP32 serial monitor
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v5.4/ukf_vs_ekf.py
Error     : Outlier rejection drops 100% of measurements
Terminal  : ESP32 serial monitor
  $ python3 ukf_vs_ekf.py
  accepted: 0/48 measurements
  pose drifts with no updates
WHAT HAPPENED
  The filter never updated - every single measurement was rejected as an outlier. The robot moved, but the pose estimate just drifted open-loop.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The Mahalanobis gate used chi-square threshold 3 (about 1 sigma) for a measurement that legitimately carries 2-3 sigma noise. With the gate set tighter than the noise, every genuine reading exceeded the threshold and was discarded. Outlier rejection assumes the model matches the noise; a gate calibrated for a different sensor or surface rejects the true signal as noise.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by raising the gate to chi-square 9 (3 sigma), then validating with the outlier_test that at least 95% of genuine measurements pass.

E0540 | v5.4 | BIG | Found Day 90 | Fixed in 5 days | Pi SSH terminal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v5.4/ukf_vs_ekf.py
Error     : Motor interference corrupts the IMU bus
Terminal  : Pi SSH terminal
  imu: all zeros every 3rd frame
  motor on = imu errors
WHAT HAPPENED
  The IMU readings became periodic zeros whenever the motors ran hard. With the motors off, the IMU was perfect - the interference was directly observable.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The motor current creates electromagnetic interference that coupled into the unshielded I2C wires, corrupting transfers when the throttle rose. I2C has no error detection on the data line, so a corrupted frame is read as valid data - zeros were the corruption pattern. The failure scaled with current, exactly like a conducted EMI problem.
INVESTIGATION (before the fix)
  - Ran the motor_interference_test - errors tracked throttle exactly
  - Measured the noise on the I2C lines with a scope
  - Routed the wires away from the motor cables - errors vanished
FIX (took 5 days)
  Fixed by rerouting the I2C wiring away from the motor power cables, adding a ground shield, and treating all-zero IMU frames as invalid in the fusion layer.

  actual: x=1.8 y=2.0 theta=0.0

  - Bounded the noise growth and re-ran - divergence gone

  Fixed by bounding the adaptive noise growth to a maximum factor, and by adding a sanity gate that falls back to the EKF when the UKF and EKF disagree by more than 1m.

E0553 | v5.6 | SMALL | Found Day 93 | Fixed in 1 day | systemd journal

File      : history/v5.6/adaptive_noise.py
Error     : Cross-verify reports 40cm disagreement
Terminal  : systemd journal
  $ python3 adaptive_noise.py
  tof=0.82m  camera=0.42m  diff=0.40m

WHAT HAPPENED
  The ToF and camera distance estimates disagreed by 40cm on the same target. One of them was right; the cross-verify test existed precisely to find which.

E0554 | v5.6 | SMALL | Found Day 93 | Fixed in 1 day | systemd journal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v5.6/surface_test.py
Error     : EKF linearization fails on sharp turns
Terminal  : systemd journal
  $ python3 surface_test.py
  ekf error: Jacobian is zero
  state: x=0.5 y=2.1 theta=nan
WHAT HAPPENED
  The EKF produced NaN heading on sharp turns. The filter worked on gentle curves and fell apart on the aggressive ones.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The EKF linearizes the motion model with a Jacobian evaluated at the current state. For a sharp turn the yaw Jacobian term was dropped in the model, so the Jacobian row became zero and the state transition lost its heading information - the estimate collapsed to NaN. The EKF's approximation quality depends on the Jacobian being accurate; a model simplified for straight driving is invalid at large steering angles.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by adding the missing yaw-dynamics term to the Jacobian and extending the ekf_test with a sharp-turn scenario.

E0555 | v5.6 | SMALL | Found Day 93 | Fixed in 1 day | systemd journal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v5.6/adaptive_noise.py
Error     : np.linalg.LinAlgError: Singular matrix
Terminal  : systemd journal
  $ python3 adaptive_noise.py
    File "adaptive_noise.py", line 92, in update
      K = P @ H @ inv(S)
  np.linalg.LinAlgError: Singular matrix
WHAT HAPPENED
  The UKF crashed on its first update with all sensors dead. The innovation covariance was singular - the filter had no information at all.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  With every sensor returning zero, the innovation covariance S became singular (determinant zero), and matrix inversion is undefined for singular matrices. The UKF assumes measurements carry some information; all-zero measurements violate that assumption. Mathematically this is the filter asking for the inverse of a zero matrix - the error is the correct behavior of the math, and the bug is that nothing prevented it.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by checking the condition number of S before the update and skipping the update when it exceeds a threshold, keeping the prediction only.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
E0556 | v5.6 | SMALL | Found Day 93 | Fixed in 1 day | systemd journal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v5.6/surface_test.py
Error     : NaN appears in the covariance matrix
Terminal  : systemd journal
  $ python3 surface_test.py
  P = [[nan nan],[nan nan]]
  pose estimate frozen
WHAT HAPPENED
  The covariance matrix filled with NaN and the pose stopped updating. The filter neither crashed nor recovered - it just froze.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  One corrupted measurement (a 0 divided during normalization) introduced NaN into the state, and every subsequent update propagated it through the linear algebra. The UKF has no built-in NaN detection; NaN arithmetic silently poisons every matrix product. The failure showed up minutes later as a frozen pose, long after the bad sample was long gone.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by validating every measurement with np.isfinite() before the update and rejecting non-finite samples with a logged warning.

E0557 | v5.6 | SMALL | Found Day 93 | Fixed in 1 day | systemd journal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v5.6/adaptive_noise.py
Error     : Negative variance in the dead reckoning
Terminal  : systemd journal
  $ python3 adaptive_noise.py
  variance: -0.004
  sigma = nan
WHAT HAPPENED
  The dead-reckoning output contained a negative variance, and the standard deviation computed from it became NaN. The motion estimate was mathematically impossible.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The noise model added a negative correction term after a wheel-slip event - slip reduces the estimated speed, and the speed-dependent noise formula produced a negative variance. Variance is defined as the expected squared deviation, which cannot be negative; the formula was wrong for the slip regime. Negative variance then breaks the sqrt used for the 1-sigma bound.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by clamping the variance to a minimum of 1e-6 and adding an assertion in tests that the variance never leaves the valid domain.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
E0558 | v5.6 | SMALL | Found Day 93 | Fixed in 1 day | systemd journal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v5.6/surface_test.py
Error     : Outlier rejection drops 100% of measurements
Terminal  : systemd journal
  $ python3 surface_test.py
  accepted: 0/48 measurements
  pose drifts with no updates
WHAT HAPPENED
  The filter never updated - every single measurement was rejected as an outlier. The robot moved, but the pose estimate just drifted open-loop.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The Mahalanobis gate used chi-square threshold 3 (about 1 sigma) for a measurement that legitimately carries 2-3 sigma noise. With the gate set tighter than the noise, every genuine reading exceeded the threshold and was discarded. Outlier rejection assumes the model matches the noise; a gate calibrated for a different sensor or surface rejects the true signal as noise.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by raising the gate to chi-square 9 (3 sigma), then validating with the outlier_test that at least 95% of genuine measurements pass.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
E0559 | v5.6 | SMALL | Found Day 93 | Fixed in 1 day | systemd journal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v5.6/adaptive_noise.py
Error     : UKF alpha/beta/kappa parameter typo
Terminal  : systemd journal
  $ python3 adaptive_noise.py
  ukf_params.json: alpha=1e-3 beta=2 kappa=1
  filter diverges on the first turn
WHAT HAPPENED
  The UKF diverged instantly on the first corner. The same data worked with the old parameters, so the filter itself was fine - the tuning was not.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The sigma-point spread parameter alpha controls how far the sigma points lie from the mean. alpha=1e-3 collapsed the sigma points almost onto the mean, so the filter's covariance estimate was tiny and it over-trusted its state. On the first turn the innovation was huge relative to that shrunken covariance, and the correction pulled the state wildly off. One digit in a JSON file changed the filter's behavior completely.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by restoring alpha=1e-2 from the tuning run and adding a startup check that alpha is within the valid (0,1] range.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
E0560 | v5.6 | SMALL | Found Day 93 | Fixed in 1 day | systemd journal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v5.6/surface_test.py
Error     : Mag heading jumps 180 degrees on reversal
Terminal  : systemd journal
  $ python3 surface_test.py
  heading: 45 -> 225 (robot didn't turn)
  hard-iron offset missing
WHAT HAPPENED
  The heading readout flipped by exactly 180 degrees whenever the robot reversed direction. The robot never turned, but the compass said it had.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The hard-iron offset (the fixed magnetic distortion from the battery and wiring) was only applied in forward direction code paths. When reversing, the un-compensated raw vector rotated the heading by the offset magnitude - which here was almost exactly 180 degrees. The magnetometer measures the sum of the Earth field plus the constant distortion; without subtracting the distortion the heading formula is wrong.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by applying the calibrated hard-iron offset in both directions and adding the reverse path to the heading test cases.

E0561 | v5.6 | BIG | Found Day 94 | Fixed in 2 days | Pi SSH terminal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v5.6/adaptive_noise.py
Error     : Attitude flips 180 degrees during fast yaw
Terminal  : Pi SSH terminal
  roll: 0 -> 180 (fast yaw)
  gimbal lock in Euler representation
WHAT HAPPENED
  During a fast turn the reported roll flipped from 0 to 180 degrees. The robot never rolled at all - the representation of the attitude broke, not the robot.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The attitude was stored as Euler angles (roll, pitch, yaw). Euler angles suffer gimbal lock: when the pitch approaches 90 degrees, roll and yaw become the same axis and the representation degenerates, producing 180-degree jumps. The physical attitude was continuous; the Euler representation made it discontinuous. This is a mathematical property of the representation, not a sensor or filter bug.
INVESTIGATION (before the fix)
  - Replayed the attitude - the flip coincided exactly with the yaw peak
  - Tested the same motion in simulation - the flip reproduced
  - Switched to quaternion storage - the flip vanished
FIX (took 2 days)
  Fixed by switching the attitude storage to quaternions, converting to Euler only for display, and adding a unit-quaternion normalization after every update.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
E0562 | v5.6 | BIG | Found Day 94 | Fixed in 3 days | Pi SSH terminal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v5.6/surface_test.py
Error     : Motor interference corrupts the IMU bus
Terminal  : Pi SSH terminal
  imu: all zeros every 3rd frame
  motor on = imu errors
WHAT HAPPENED
  The IMU readings became periodic zeros whenever the motors ran hard. With the motors off, the IMU was perfect - the interference was directly observable.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The motor current creates electromagnetic interference that coupled into the unshielded I2C wires, corrupting transfers when the throttle rose. I2C has no error detection on the data line, so a corrupted frame is read as valid data - zeros were the corruption pattern. The failure scaled with current, exactly like a conducted EMI problem.
INVESTIGATION (before the fix)
  - Ran the motor_interference_test - errors tracked throttle exactly
  - Measured the noise on the I2C lines with a scope
  - Routed the wires away from the motor cables - errors vanished
FIX (took 3 days)
  Fixed by rerouting the I2C wiring away from the motor power cables, adding a ground shield, and treating all-zero IMU frames as invalid in the fusion layer.

E0563 | v5.6 | BIG | Found Day 94 | Fixed in 4 days | Pi SSH terminal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v5.6/adaptive_noise.py
Error     : UKF diverges and the robot drives off the track
Terminal  : Pi SSH terminal
  ukf: x=3.2 y=8.9 theta=2.1
  actual: x=1.8 y=2.0 theta=0.0
  UKF diverged, EKF fallback used
WHAT HAPPENED
  The robot drove off the track because the UKF believed the robot was somewhere else entirely. The pose was confident, detailed - and completely wrong.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The adaptive noise module grew the process noise with each suspicious measurement, and the filter's confidence in the state shrank with it. With enough noise inflation the filter trusted every new measurement blindly, and a single bad sensor reading dragged the pose far from reality. The adaptive mechanism had no upper bound on the noise it would tolerate - it adapted itself into failure.
INVESTIGATION (before the fix)
  - Plotted the UKF pose against the known track - divergence was gradual
  - Tracked the process noise growth over the run
  - Bounded the noise growth and re-ran - divergence gone
FIX (took 4 days)
  Fixed by bounding the adaptive noise growth to a maximum factor, and by adding a sanity gate that falls back to the EKF when the UKF and EKF disagree by more than 1m.

E0564 | v5.6 | BIG | Found Day 94 | Fixed in 5 days | Pi SSH terminal

Error     : Dead reckoning drifts 30cm per lap
Terminal  : Pi SSH terminal
  dead reckoning: -0.30m off after 1 lap
  wheel slip on the carpet
WHAT HAPPENED
  The dead-reckoned position was 30cm off after every lap. The error was consistent, which made it diagnosable - and unavoidable without external reference.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  Odometry assumes the wheels roll without slipping, but the carpet caused a consistent 3% slip that odometry cannot measure - it only counts rotations. Over a 10m lap, 3% is exactly 30cm.   - Computed the implied slip percentage - 3%, consistent
  - Fused the ToF wall distance as a lateral reference

  Fixed by fusing the ToF wall distance into the lateral state, so the drift is corrected by an absolute reference instead of a second integration.

E0584 | v5.8 | SMALL | Found Day 97 | Fixed in 1 day | Pi SSH terminal

Terminal  : Pi SSH terminal

  state: x=0.5 y=2.1 theta=nan
WHAT HAPPENED
  The EKF produced NaN heading on sharp turns. The filter worked on gentle curves and fell apart on the aggressive ones.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)

  The robot drove off the track because the UKF believed the robot was somewhere else entirely. The pose was confident, detailed - and completely wrong.

WHAT HAPPENED

    File "pose_pipeline.py", line 92, in update
      K = P @ H @ inv(S)
  np.linalg.LinAlgError: Singular matrix
WHAT HAPPENED
  The UKF crashed on its first update with all sensors dead. The innovation covariance was singular - the filter had no information at all.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  With every sensor returning zero, the innovation covariance S became singular (determinant zero), and matrix inversion is undefined for singular matrices. Terminal  : ESP32 serial monitor
  $ python3 motor_pid.py
  steer: +12 -14 +11 -13 deg
  no progress toward the goal
WHAT HAPPENED
  The robot wobbled in front of an obstacle without making progress. The steering command swung positive and negative every half second.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)

----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v6.0/motor_pid.py
Error     : PID output saturates then overcorrects
Terminal  : ESP32 serial monitor
  $ python3 motor_pid.py
  output: 0.98 -> -0.99 -> 0.97
  robot snakes down the straight
WHAT HAPPENED
  The robot weaved down the straight at every launch. The PID output swung from full throttle to full brake and back, several times per second.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The integral term accumulated while the robot was stalled at launch, and by the time motion started the integral alone exceeded the output limits. The controller then had to burn off the stored error by overshooting in the opposite direction - classic integral windup. Windup happens because the integrator keeps summing even while the output is clamped at its physical limit, so the error it stores is never realizable.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by adding anti-windup: stop integrating when the output is saturated and the integral would push it further into the limit.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
E0608 | v6.0 | SMALL | Found Day 101 | Fixed in 1 day | ESP32 serial monitor
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v6.0/pid_calibrate.py
Error     : Stanley cross-track error is NaN at waypoint 0
Terminal  : ESP32 serial monitor
  $ python3 pid_calibrate.py
  cross_track: nan  (first waypoint)
  no steering command sent
WHAT HAPPENED
  The Stanley controller produced no steering command at the first waypoint. The cross-track error was NaN, so the controller output was NaN, and the car drove straight past the path.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The first path segment had zero length - two identical waypoints at the start of the list - so the tangent direction was undefined, and the cross-track math divided by zero. Stanley's formula assumes a valid segment direction; a zero-length segment violates that invariant. The NaN then propagated through the control output because no validation existed between the path math and the steering command.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by skipping zero-length segments in the path parser and replacing any NaN cross-track value with the previous valid value.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
E0609 | v6.0 | BIG | Found Day 102 | Fixed in 2 days | Pi SSH terminal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v6.0/motor_pid.py
Error     : Global planner returns a path through the pillar
Terminal  : Pi SSH terminal
  $ python3 motor_pid.py
  path waypoint 3: inside the pillar
  collision on the replay
WHAT HAPPENED
  The global planner produced a path that ran straight through a pillar. The replay showed the collision clearly - the planner never considered the robot's width.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The grid cost map marked only the obstacle's exact cells as blocked. A robot has physical width, so its center can be up to half a width away from an obstacle while the robot still collides. The planner used a point model for a 20cm-wide robot. Path planning for a real robot requires the configuration-space inflation; planning a point path through the environment is planning a point's path.
INVESTIGATION (before the fix)
  - Replayed the planned path against the map - the waypoint was inside
  - Measured the clearance at the collision - less than the robot width
  - Inflated the obstacles by the robot radius and re-planned
FIX (took 2 days)
  Fixed by inflating all obstacles by the robot radius before running A*, and adding a clearance check on the final path.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
E0610 | v6.0 | BIG | Found Day 102 | Fixed in 3 days | Pi SSH terminal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v6.0/pid_calibrate.py
Error     : Velocity profile ignores the corner limit
Terminal  : Pi SSH terminal
  $ python3 pid_calibrate.py
  v = 2.0 m/s into a 60-degree corner
  tire squeal, robot drifts
WHAT HAPPENED
  The robot entered a 60-degree corner at full speed and slid wide. The profile optimized for time with no regard for what the tires can do.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The velocity profile minimized lap time subject only to acceleration limits, not to lateral acceleration. A corner has a speed limit set by physics: v_max = sqrt(mu * g * r). Ignoring the curvature limit produced a profile that is fast on paper and impossible in reality - the tires physically cannot provide the required lateral force.
INVESTIGATION (before the fix)
  - Measured the actual cornering speed limit on the track
  - Overlaid the profile's speed at the corner - it exceeded the limit
  - Added a curvature-dependent speed cap to the profile
FIX (took 3 days)
  Fixed by adding a speed cap derived from the path curvature and the measured tire limit, applied at every point of the profile.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
E0611 | v6.0 | BIG | Found Day 102 | Fixed in 4 days | Pi SSH terminal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v6.0/motor_pid.py
Error     : Cubic spline path is jerky at waypoint 5
Terminal  : Pi SSH terminal
  $ python3 motor_pid.py
  acceleration spike: 12 m/s^2 at wp5
  visible jerk in the run
WHAT HAPPENED
  At waypoint 5 the robot jerked visibly. The path was smooth to the eye - the jerk was in the timing, not the shape.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The spline was parameterized by a non-arc-length parameter, so equal parameter steps cover unequal distances along the path. The velocity controller interpreted parameter speed as spatial speed, producing huge accelerations where the parameterization compressed distance. A geometrically smooth path can be dynamically jerky if the parameterization is uneven.
INVESTIGATION (before the fix)
  - Plotted the path speed against distance - the spike matched wp5
  - Checked the parameterization - it was not arc length
  - Reparameterized by arc length and re-ran
FIX (took 4 days)
  Fixed by reparameterizing the spline with arc length so parameter speed equals spatial speed, and validating the acceleration profile in the profile_test.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
E0612 | v6.0 | BIG | Found Day 102 | Fixed in 5 days | Pi SSH terminal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v6.0/pid_calibrate.py
Error     : Feedforward causes overshoot in sharp turns
Terminal  : Pi SSH terminal
  $ python3 pid_calibrate.py
  ff: +0.8 -> overshoot 8 degrees
  corrective jerk after each corner
WHAT HAPPENED
  After every sharp corner the robot overshot the heading by 8 degrees and then corrected with a jerk. Gentle corners were fine - only the sharp ones overshot.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The feedforward gain was tuned for the average curve and over-applied on sharp ones. The steering response is nonlinear: at large angles the servo linkage has different leverage, so a feedforward command calibrated for 30 degrees is too strong at 90. A single constant gain cannot fit a nonlinear plant across the whole operating range.
INVESTIGATION (before the fix)
  - Measured the overshoot against corner sharpness - it scaled with angle
  - Plotted the steer response vs command - nonlinear above 45 degrees
  - Scaled the feedforward with the corner curvature
FIX (took 5 days)
  Fixed by scaling the feedforward with the path curvature, and verifying with the corner_test that the overshoot stays under 2 degrees.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
E0613 | v6.1 | SMALL | Found Day 103 | Fixed in 1 day | Windows CMD
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v6.1/servo_pid.py
Error     : Feedforward sign is opposite on reverse
Terminal  : Windows CMD
  $ python3 servo_pid.py
  reverse + feedforward = wrong direction
  robot pulls to the left in reverse
WHAT HAPPENED
  In reverse, the robot consistently pulled to the left. The feedback controller was compensating correctly - the feedforward term was actively fighting it.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The feedforward steering term was computed for forward motion and applied unchanged when reversing. Steering geometry is direction-dependent: the same curvature requires the opposite steer correction when the velocity is negative. The sign flip was known in the ackermann module but not propagated to the controller, so two modules disagreed about the direction convention.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by multiplying the feedforward term by the direction sign, and adding a reverse-path test case to the controller test suite.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
E0614 | v6.1 | SMALL | Found Day 103 | Fixed in 1 day | Windows CMD
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v6.1/servo_step_test.py
Error     : Cubic spline overshoots past the goal
Terminal  : Windows CMD
  $ python3 servo_step_test.py
  end: x=2.01 y=0.03 (goal 2.00, 0.00)
  overshoot 1cm at the parking spot
WHAT HAPPENED
  The spline ended 1cm past the parking target. Small in absolute terms, fatal for a parking maneuver where the tolerance is measured in millimeters.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The smoothing pass relaxed the endpoint constraints, letting the spline drift off the fixed end point. Splines are defined by their boundary conditions; the endpoint condition was applied before smoothing and the smoother was allowed to move it. The constraint was lost in the pipeline, not in the math.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by re-imposing the fixed endpoint condition after smoothing and adding a unit test that pins both endpoints to the exact goal.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
E0615 | v6.1 | SMALL | Found Day 103 | Fixed in 1 day | Windows CMD
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v6.1/servo_pid.py
Error     : Velocity profile outputs negative speeds
Terminal  : Windows CMD
  $ python3 servo_pid.py
  v: -0.2 m/s at t=1.2s
  robot reverses mid-run
WHAT HAPPENED
  The robot briefly reversed in the middle of a straight run. The velocity profile commanded a negative speed - the robot was doing exactly what it was told.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The trapezoidal profile computes the deceleration phase assuming the target is reachable in the given time. When the target was too close for the time budget, the deceleration term overshot below zero. The math produced an unreachable profile instead of detecting the conflict; negative speed is the profile's way of saying 'the plan is impossible'.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by clamping the profile speed to zero and extending the profile duration when the target is not reachable within the requested time.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
E0616 | v6.1 | SMALL | Found Day 103 | Fixed in 1 day | Windows CMD
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v6.1/servo_step_test.py
Error     : Obstacle avoidance oscillates left-right
Terminal  : Windows CMD
  $ python3 servo_step_test.py
  steer: +12 -14 +11 -13 deg
  no progress toward the goal
WHAT HAPPENED
  The robot wobbled in front of an obstacle without making progress. The steering command swung positive and negative every half second.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The avoidance gain and the goal-pull gain fought each other: as the robot turned away from the obstacle it aligned with the goal, and as it turned toward the goal it approached the obstacle again. Two competing controllers with no arbitration produced a limit cycle. The oscillation is the system's equilibrium - it is stable in the wrong way.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by adding a deadband where neither controller acts and a goal bias that makes the goal-pull dominant whenever both demands conflict.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
E0617 | v6.1 | SMALL | Found Day 103 | Fixed in 1 day | Windows CMD
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v6.1/servo_pid.py
Error     : MPC solve fails on the first step
Terminal  : Windows CMD
  $ python3 servo_pid.py
  cvxpy error: Problem status INFEASIBLE
  no control output
WHAT HAPPENED
  The model-predictive controller produced no output at all - the solver reported the optimization problem was infeasible at the very first step.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The MPC horizon covered more track than existed, and the terminal constraint required the robot to be at a goal point the path could not reach within the horizon. A constrained optimization with contradictory constraints is infeasible by definition; the solver correctly refused to solve an impossible problem. The model was the bug - the horizon and constraints did not match the track geometry.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by shrinking the horizon to the track length and relaxing the terminal constraint from an equality to a soft penalty.

E0620 | v6.1 | SMALL | Found Day 103 | Fixed in 1 day | Windows CMD
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v6.1/servo_step_test.py
Error     : Gain schedule jumps at the speed boundary
Terminal  : Windows CMD
  $ python3 servo_step_test.py
  gain: 0.9 -> 2.4 (speed 1.00 m/s)
  steering step visible in the log
WHAT HAPPENED
  The steering gain jumped from 0.9 to 2.4 the instant the robot crossed 1 m/s. The steering response suddenly felt twice as aggressive.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The gain schedule was a lookup table with discrete rows, and the lookup switched rows at the boundary instead of interpolating between them. A discontinuous gain produces a discontinuous control law: the controller's personality changes instantly at a speed threshold. Gain scheduling is only smooth when the schedule itself is smooth.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by linearly interpolating between table rows, and adding a test that verifies the gain never changes by more than 10% per control tick.

E0624 | v6.1 | BIG | Found Day 104 | Fixed in 5 days | Pi SSH terminal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v6.1/servo_step_test.py
Error     : Anti-windup test fails with 30% overshoot
Terminal  : Pi SSH terminal
  $ python3 servo_step_test.py
  overshoot: 30% (target <10%)
  anti-windup not active
WHAT HAPPENED
  The windup test measured 30% overshoot - three times the target. The anti-windup code existed, was enabled, and did nothing.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The saturation check inside the anti-windup compared the output against the wrong limits - the controller's nominal range instead of the physical PWM limits. The controller output could never exceed its nominal range, so the saturation detector never triggered, so the anti-windup was permanently inactive. The feature was dead code with its documentation claiming otherwise.
INVESTIGATION (before the fix)
  - Read the windup_test output - the saturation flag never fired
  - Compared the check limits with the real PWM limits - they differed
  - Fixed the limits and re-ran - overshoot dropped to 4%
FIX (took 5 days)
  Fixed by comparing against the physical PWM limits in the saturation check, and adding a test assertion that the anti-windup flag actually activates during a stall.

  - Measured the overshoot against corner sharpness - it scaled with angle
  - Plotted the steer response vs command - nonlinear above 45 degrees
  - Scaled the feedforward with the corner curvature
FIX (took 3 days)
  Fixed by scaling the feedforward with the path curvature, and verifying with the corner_test that the overshoot stays under 2 degrees.

E0635 | v6.2 | BIG | Found Day 106 | Fixed in 4 days | Pi SSH terminal

File      : history/v6.2/stanley_tune.py
Error     : Anti-windup test fails with 30% overshoot
Terminal  : Pi SSH terminal
  $ python3 stanley_tune.py
  overshoot: 30% (target <10%)
  anti-windup not active
WHAT HAPPENED
  The windup test measured 30% overshoot - three times the target. The anti-windup code existed, was enabled, and did nothing.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)

E0636 | v6.2 | BIG | Found Day 106 | Fixed in 5 days | Pi SSH terminal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v6.2/stanley.py
Error     : Obstacle avoidance deadlocks in a U-shaped trap
Terminal  : Pi SSH terminal
  $ python3 stanley.py
  avoid: stuck 12s at the same spot
  no escape direction found
WHAT HAPPENED
  The robot stood inside a U-shaped arrangement for 12 seconds, unable to leave. Every direction it evaluated was blocked - by its own previous decisions.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  Local avoidance is greedy: it always chooses the best direction now. Inside a U-shape every local direction leads back inside, so the robot oscillates between two bad options forever. Without memory of where it has been, the planner cannot know it is looping. The U-shape is the classic deadlock of purely local planning.
INVESTIGATION (before the fix)
  - Logged the chosen direction over time - it alternated between two
  - Verified a memory of visited positions breaks the loop
  - Added a heading memory that penalizes recently visited directions
FIX (took 5 days)
  Fixed by adding a small heading memory that penalizes directions tried in the last 3 seconds, forcing the planner to commit to one escape direction.

E0637 | v6.3 | SMALL | Found Day 107 | Fixed in 1 day | VS Code terminal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v6.3/corner_test.py
Error     : Velocity profile outputs negative speeds
Terminal  : VS Code terminal
  $ python3 corner_test.py
  v: -0.2 m/s at t=1.2s
  robot reverses mid-run
WHAT HAPPENED
  The robot briefly reversed in the middle of a straight run. The velocity profile commanded a negative speed - the robot was doing exactly what it was told.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The trapezoidal profile computes the deceleration phase assuming the target is reachable in the given time. When the target was too close for the time budget, the deceleration term overshot below zero. The math produced an unreachable profile instead of detecting the conflict; negative speed is the profile's way of saying 'the plan is impossible'.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by clamping the profile speed to zero and extending the profile duration when the target is not reachable within the requested time.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
E0638 | v6.3 | SMALL | Found Day 107 | Fixed in 1 day | VS Code terminal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v6.3/feedforward_steer.py
Error     : Obstacle avoidance oscillates left-right
Terminal  : VS Code terminal
  $ python3 feedforward_steer.py
  steer: +12 -14 +11 -13 deg
  no progress toward the goal
WHAT HAPPENED
  The robot wobbled in front of an obstacle without making progress. The steering command swung positive and negative every half second.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The avoidance gain and the goal-pull gain fought each other: as the robot turned away from the obstacle it aligned with the goal, and as it turned toward the goal it approached the obstacle again. Two competing controllers with no arbitration produced a limit cycle. The oscillation is the system's equilibrium - it is stable in the wrong way.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by adding a deadband where neither controller acts and a goal bias that makes the goal-pull dominant whenever both demands conflict.

E0639 | v6.3 | SMALL | Found Day 107 | Fixed in 1 day | VS Code terminal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v6.3/corner_test.py
Error     : MPC solve fails on the first step
Terminal  : VS Code terminal
  $ python3 corner_test.py
  cvxpy error: Problem status INFEASIBLE
  no control output
WHAT HAPPENED
  The model-predictive controller produced no output at all - the solver reported the optimization problem was infeasible at the very first step.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The MPC horizon covered more track than existed, and the terminal constraint required the robot to be at a goal point the path could not reach within the horizon. A constrained optimization with contradictory constraints is infeasible by definition; the solver correctly refused to solve an impossible problem. The model was the bug - the horizon and constraints did not match the track geometry.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by shrinking the horizon to the track length and relaxing the terminal constraint from an equality to a soft penalty.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
E0640 | v6.3 | SMALL | Found Day 107 | Fixed in 1 day | VS Code terminal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v6.3/feedforward_steer.py
Error     : PID output saturates then overcorrects
Terminal  : VS Code terminal
  $ python3 feedforward_steer.py
  output: 0.98 -> -0.99 -> 0.97
  robot snakes down the straight
WHAT HAPPENED
  The robot weaved down the straight at every launch. The PID output swung from full throttle to full brake and back, several times per second.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The integral term accumulated while the robot was stalled at launch, and by the time motion started the integral alone exceeded the output limits. The controller then had to burn off the stored error by overshooting in the opposite direction - classic integral windup. Windup happens because the integrator keeps summing even while the output is clamped at its physical limit, so the error it stores is never realizable.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by adding anti-windup: stop integrating when the output is saturated and the integral would push it further into the limit.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
E0641 | v6.3 | SMALL | Found Day 107 | Fixed in 1 day | VS Code terminal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v6.3/corner_test.py
Error     : Stanley cross-track error is NaN at waypoint 0
Terminal  : VS Code terminal
  $ python3 corner_test.py
  cross_track: nan  (first waypoint)
  no steering command sent
WHAT HAPPENED
  The Stanley controller produced no steering command at the first waypoint. The cross-track error was NaN, so the controller output was NaN, and the car drove straight past the path.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The first path segment had zero length - two identical waypoints at the start of the list - so the tangent direction was undefined, and the cross-track math divided by zero. Stanley's formula assumes a valid segment direction; a zero-length segment violates that invariant. The NaN then propagated through the control output because no validation existed between the path math and the steering command.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by skipping zero-length segments in the path parser and replacing any NaN cross-track value with the previous valid value.

E0642 | v6.3 | SMALL | Found Day 107 | Fixed in 1 day | VS Code terminal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v6.3/feedforward_steer.py
Error     : Gain schedule jumps at the speed boundary
Terminal  : VS Code terminal
  $ python3 feedforward_steer.py
  gain: 0.9 -> 2.4 (speed 1.00 m/s)
  steering step visible in the log
WHAT HAPPENED
  The steering gain jumped from 0.9 to 2.4 the instant the robot crossed 1 m/s. The steering response suddenly felt twice as aggressive.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The gain schedule was a lookup table with discrete rows, and the lookup switched rows at the boundary instead of interpolating between them. A discontinuous gain produces a discontinuous control law: the controller's personality changes instantly at a speed threshold. Gain scheduling is only smooth when the schedule itself is smooth.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by linearly interpolating between table rows, and adding a test that verifies the gain never changes by more than 10% per control tick.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
E0643 | v6.3 | SMALL | Found Day 107 | Fixed in 1 day | VS Code terminal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v6.3/corner_test.py
Error     : Feedforward sign is opposite on reverse
Terminal  : VS Code terminal
  $ python3 corner_test.py
  reverse + feedforward = wrong direction
  robot pulls to the left in reverse
WHAT HAPPENED
  In reverse, the robot consistently pulled to the left. The feedback controller was compensating correctly - the feedforward term was actively fighting it.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The feedforward steering term was computed for forward motion and applied unchanged when reversing. Steering geometry is direction-dependent: the same curvature requires the opposite steer correction when the velocity is negative. The sign flip was known in the ackermann module but not propagated to the controller, so two modules disagreed about the direction convention.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by multiplying the feedforward term by the direction sign, and adding a reverse-path test case to the controller test suite.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
E0644 | v6.3 | SMALL | Found Day 107 | Fixed in 1 day | VS Code terminal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v6.3/feedforward_steer.py
Error     : Cubic spline overshoots past the goal
Terminal  : VS Code terminal
  $ python3 feedforward_steer.py
  end: x=2.01 y=0.03 (goal 2.00, 0.00)
  overshoot 1cm at the parking spot
WHAT HAPPENED
  The spline ended 1cm past the parking target. Small in absolute terms, fatal for a parking maneuver where the tolerance is measured in millimeters.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The smoothing pass relaxed the endpoint constraints, letting the spline drift off the fixed end point. Splines are defined by their boundary conditions; the endpoint condition was applied before smoothing and the smoother was allowed to move it. The constraint was lost in the pipeline, not in the math.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by re-imposing the fixed endpoint condition after smoothing and adding a unit test that pins both endpoints to the exact goal.

E0662 | v6.5 | SMALL | Found Day 111 | Fixed in 1 day | Pi console (HDMI)
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v6.5/windup_test.py
Error     : PID output saturates then overcorrects
Terminal  : Pi console (HDMI)
  $ python3 windup_test.py
  output: 0.98 -> -0.99 -> 0.97
  robot snakes down the straight
WHAT HAPPENED
  The robot weaved down the straight at every launch. The PID output swung from full throttle to full brake and back, several times per second.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The integral term accumulated while the robot was stalled at launch, and by the time motion started the integral alone exceeded the output limits. The controller then had to burn off the stored error by overshooting in the opposite direction - classic integral windup. Windup happens because the integrator keeps summing even while the output is clamped at its physical limit, so the error it stores is never realizable.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by adding anti-windup: stop integrating when the output is saturated and the integral would push it further into the limit.

E0663 | v6.5 | SMALL | Found Day 111 | Fixed in 1 day | Pi console (HDMI)
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v6.5/anti_windup.py
Error     : Stanley cross-track error is NaN at waypoint 0
Terminal  : Pi console (HDMI)
  $ python3 anti_windup.py
  cross_track: nan  (first waypoint)
  no steering command sent
WHAT HAPPENED
  The Stanley controller produced no steering command at the first waypoint. The cross-track error was NaN, so the controller output was NaN, and the car drove straight past the path.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The first path segment had zero length - two identical waypoints at the start of the list - so the tangent direction was undefined, and the cross-track math divided by zero. Stanley's formula assumes a valid segment direction; a zero-length segment violates that invariant. The NaN then propagated through the control output because no validation existed between the path math and the steering command.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by skipping zero-length segments in the path parser and replacing any NaN cross-track value with the previous valid value.

E0664 | v6.5 | SMALL | Found Day 111 | Fixed in 1 day | Pi console (HDMI)
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v6.5/windup_test.py
Error     : Gain schedule jumps at the speed boundary
Terminal  : Pi console (HDMI)
  $ python3 windup_test.py
  gain: 0.9 -> 2.4 (speed 1.00 m/s)
  steering step visible in the log
WHAT HAPPENED
  The steering gain jumped from 0.9 to 2.4 the instant the robot crossed 1 m/s. The steering response suddenly felt twice as aggressive.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The gain schedule was a lookup table with discrete rows, and the lookup switched rows at the boundary instead of interpolating between them. A discontinuous gain produces a discontinuous control law: the controller's personality changes instantly at a speed threshold. Gain scheduling is only smooth when the schedule itself is smooth.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by linearly interpolating between table rows, and adding a test that verifies the gain never changes by more than 10% per control tick.

E0665 | v6.5 | SMALL | Found Day 111 | Fixed in 1 day | Pi console (HDMI)
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v6.5/anti_windup.py
Error     : Feedforward sign is opposite on reverse
Terminal  : Pi console (HDMI)
  $ python3 anti_windup.py
  reverse + feedforward = wrong direction
  robot pulls to the left in reverse
WHAT HAPPENED
  In reverse, the robot consistently pulled to the left. The feedback controller was compensating correctly - the feedforward term was actively fighting it.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The feedforward steering term was computed for forward motion and applied unchanged when reversing. Steering geometry is direction-dependent: the same curvature requires the opposite steer correction when the velocity is negative. The sign flip was known in the ackermann module but not propagated to the controller, so two modules disagreed about the direction convention.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by multiplying the feedforward term by the direction sign, and adding a reverse-path test case to the controller test suite.

E0666 | v6.5 | SMALL | Found Day 111 | Fixed in 1 day | Pi console (HDMI)
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v6.5/windup_test.py
Error     : Cubic spline overshoots past the goal
Terminal  : Pi console (HDMI)
  $ python3 windup_test.py
  end: x=2.01 y=0.03 (goal 2.00, 0.00)
  overshoot 1cm at the parking spot
WHAT HAPPENED
  The spline ended 1cm past the parking target. Small in absolute terms, fatal for a parking maneuver where the tolerance is measured in millimeters.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The smoothing pass relaxed the endpoint constraints, letting the spline drift off the fixed end point. Splines are defined by their boundary conditions; the endpoint condition was applied before smoothing and the smoother was allowed to move it. The constraint was lost in the pipeline, not in the math.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by re-imposing the fixed endpoint condition after smoothing and adding a unit test that pins both endpoints to the exact goal.

E0667 | v6.5 | SMALL | Found Day 111 | Fixed in 1 day | Pi console (HDMI)
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v6.5/anti_windup.py
Error     : Velocity profile outputs negative speeds
Terminal  : Pi console (HDMI)
  $ python3 anti_windup.py
  v: -0.2 m/s at t=1.2s
  robot reverses mid-run
WHAT HAPPENED
  The robot briefly reversed in the middle of a straight run. The velocity profile commanded a negative speed - the robot was doing exactly what it was told.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The trapezoidal profile computes the deceleration phase assuming the target is reachable in the given time. When the target was too close for the time budget, the deceleration term overshot below zero. The math produced an unreachable profile instead of detecting the conflict; negative speed is the profile's way of saying 'the plan is impossible'.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by clamping the profile speed to zero and extending the profile duration when the target is not reachable within the requested time.
