E0668 | v6.5 | SMALL | Found Day 111 | Fixed in 1 day | Pi console (HDMI)
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v6.5/windup_test.py
Error     : Obstacle avoidance oscillates left-right
Terminal  : Pi console (HDMI)
  $ python3 windup_test.py
  steer: +12 -14 +11 -13 deg
  no progress toward the goal
WHAT HAPPENED
  The robot wobbled in front of an obstacle without making progress. The steering command swung positive and negative every half second.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The avoidance gain and the goal-pull gain fought each other: as the robot turned away from the obstacle it aligned with the goal, and as it turned toward the goal it approached the obstacle again. Two competing controllers with no arbitration produced a limit cycle. The oscillation is the system's equilibrium - it is stable in the wrong way.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by adding a deadband where neither controller acts and a goal bias that makes the goal-pull dominant whenever both demands conflict.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
E0669 | v6.5 | BIG | Found Day 112 | Fixed in 2 days | Pi SSH terminal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v6.5/anti_windup.py
Error     : Obstacle avoidance deadlocks in a U-shaped trap
Terminal  : Pi SSH terminal
  $ python3 anti_windup.py
  avoid: stuck 12s at the same spot
  no escape direction found
WHAT HAPPENED
  The robot stood inside a U-shaped arrangement for 12 seconds, unable to leave. Every direction it evaluated was blocked - by its own previous decisions.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  Local avoidance is greedy: it always chooses the best direction now. Inside a U-shape every local direction leads back inside, so the robot oscillates between two bad options forever. Without memory of where it has been, the planner cannot know it is looping. The U-shape is the classic deadlock of purely local planning.
INVESTIGATION (before the fix)
  - Logged the chosen direction over time - it alternated between two
  - Verified a memory of visited positions breaks the loop
  - Added a heading memory that penalizes recently visited directions
FIX (took 2 days)
  Fixed by adding a small heading memory that penalizes directions tried in the last 3 seconds, forcing the planner to commit to one escape direction.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
E0670 | v6.5 | BIG | Found Day 112 | Fixed in 3 days | Pi SSH terminal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v6.5/windup_test.py
Error     : Steering oscillates at 5Hz on the straight
Terminal  : Pi SSH terminal
  $ python3 windup_test.py
  steer: +5 -5 +5 -5 deg at 5Hz
  overshoot visible in the video
WHAT HAPPENED
  The robot wobbled down the straight at 5Hz - a visible, rhythmic steering oscillation. On the bench the servo moved perfectly; on the floor it wagged.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The servo PID gains were tuned with the wheels in the air, where there is no lateral force. On the floor the tire forces and frame compliance add dynamics that the bench never exercised, and the gains that were stable on the bench were marginal on the floor. A control loop is only as good as the model it was tuned against; tuning against the wrong plant guarantees this result.
INVESTIGATION (before the fix)
  - Recorded the oscillation and measured its frequency
  - Tested the same gains with the wheels on the floor vs in the air
  - Re-tuned with the robot on the floor using the servo_step_test
FIX (took 3 days)
  Fixed by re-tuning the servo PID with the robot on the floor, and by making the tuning procedure run on the actual competition surface.

E0671 | v6.5 | BIG | Found Day 112 | Fixed in 4 days | Pi SSH terminal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v6.5/anti_windup.py
Error     : Integral windup launches the robot at the start
Terminal  : Pi SSH terminal
  $ python3 anti_windup.py
  integral: 0 -> 3.8 during stall
  robot jumps forward 30cm
WHAT HAPPENED
  The robot jumped 30cm forward the moment it was released at the start line. The controller had been accumulating error during the stall and released it all at once.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  While the robot was held at the start, the position error was large and constant, and the integrator summed it until the output hit the limit. The moment the hold released, the saturated output was applied instantly - a launch, not a start. Windup storage is invisible until the constraint disappears, which is why it always surfaces at the worst moment.
INVESTIGATION (before the fix)
  - Logged the integral term during the stall - it grew linearly
  - Confirmed the jump magnitude matched the stored integral
  - Added integral clamping and a pre-start integral reset
FIX (took 4 days)
  Fixed by clamping the integral to the output limits and resetting it when the robot is in the hold state, so the launch is a ramp, not a step.

E0672 | v6.5 | BIG | Found Day 112 | Fixed in 5 days | Pi SSH terminal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v6.5/windup_test.py
Error     : Global planner returns a path through the pillar
Terminal  : Pi SSH terminal
  $ python3 windup_test.py
  path waypoint 3: inside the pillar
  collision on the replay
WHAT HAPPENED
  The global planner produced a path that ran straight through a pillar. The replay showed the collision clearly - the planner never considered the robot's width.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The grid cost map marked only the obstacle's exact cells as blocked. A robot has physical width, so its center can be up to half a width away from an obstacle while the robot still collides. The planner used a point model for a 20cm-wide robot. Path planning for a real robot requires the configuration-space inflation; planning a point path through the environment is planning a point's path.
INVESTIGATION (before the fix)
  - Replayed the planned path against the map - the waypoint was inside
  - Measured the clearance at the collision - less than the robot width
  - Inflated the obstacles by the robot radius and re-planned
FIX (took 5 days)
  Fixed by inflating all obstacles by the robot radius before running A*, and adding a clearance check on the final path.

Error     : MPC solve fails on the first step
Terminal  : ESP32 serial monitor
  $ python3 planner_test.py
  cvxpy error: Problem status INFEASIBLE
  no control output
WHAT HAPPENED
  The model-predictive controller produced no output at all - the solver reported the optimization problem was infeasible at the very first step.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The MPC horizon covered more track than existed, and the terminal constraint required the robot to be at a goal point the path could not reach within the horizon. A constrained optimization with contradictory constraints is infeasible by definition; the solver correctly refused to solve an impossible problem. The model was the bug - the horizon and constraints did not match the track geometry.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by shrinking the horizon to the track length and relaxing the terminal constraint from an equality to a soft penalty.

  The robot briefly reversed in the middle of a straight run. The velocity profile commanded a negative speed - the robot was doing exactly what it was told.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The trapezoidal profile computes the deceleration phase assuming the target is reachable in the given time. When the target was too close for the time budget, the deceleration term overshot below zero. The math produced an unreachable profile instead of detecting the conflict; negative speed is the profile's way of saying 'the plan is impossible'.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by clamping the profile speed to zero and extending the profile duration when the target is not reachable within the requested time.

E0690 | v6.7 | SMALL | Found Day 115 | Fixed in 1 day | Windows CMD
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v6.7/spline_visualize.py
Error     : Obstacle avoidance oscillates left-right
Terminal  : Windows CMD
  $ python3 spline_visualize.py
  steer: +12 -14 +11 -13 deg
  no progress toward the goal
WHAT HAPPENED
  The robot wobbled in front of an obstacle without making progress. The steering command swung positive and negative every half second.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The avoidance gain and the goal-pull gain fought each other: as the robot turned away from the obstacle it aligned with the goal, and as it turned toward the goal it approached the obstacle again. Two competing controllers with no arbitration produced a limit cycle. The oscillation is the system's equilibrium - it is stable in the wrong way.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by adding a deadband where neither controller acts and a goal bias that makes the goal-pull dominant whenever both demands conflict.

E0691 | v6.7 | SMALL | Found Day 115 | Fixed in 1 day | Windows CMD
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v6.7/cubic_spline.py
Error     : MPC solve fails on the first step
Terminal  : Windows CMD
  $ python3 cubic_spline.py
  cvxpy error: Problem status INFEASIBLE
  no control output
WHAT HAPPENED
  The model-predictive controller produced no output at all - the solver reported the optimization problem was infeasible at the very first step.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The MPC horizon covered more track than existed, and the terminal constraint required the robot to be at a goal point the path could not reach within the horizon. A constrained optimization with contradictory constraints is infeasible by definition; the solver correctly refused to solve an impossible problem. The model was the bug - the horizon and constraints did not match the track geometry.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by shrinking the horizon to the track length and relaxing the terminal constraint from an equality to a soft penalty.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
E0692 | v6.7 | SMALL | Found Day 115 | Fixed in 1 day | Windows CMD
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v6.7/spline_visualize.py
Error     : PID output saturates then overcorrects
Terminal  : Windows CMD
  $ python3 spline_visualize.py
  output: 0.98 -> -0.99 -> 0.97
  robot snakes down the straight
WHAT HAPPENED
  The robot weaved down the straight at every launch. The PID output swung from full throttle to full brake and back, several times per second.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The integral term accumulated while the robot was stalled at launch, and by the time motion started the integral alone exceeded the output limits. The controller then had to burn off the stored error by overshooting in the opposite direction - classic integral windup. Windup happens because the integrator keeps summing even while the output is clamped at its physical limit, so the error it stores is never realizable.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by adding anti-windup: stop integrating when the output is saturated and the integral would push it further into the limit.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
E0693 | v6.7 | BIG | Found Day 116 | Fixed in 2 days | Pi SSH terminal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v6.7/cubic_spline.py
Error     : Integral windup launches the robot at the start
Terminal  : Pi SSH terminal
  $ python3 cubic_spline.py
  integral: 0 -> 3.8 during stall
  robot jumps forward 30cm
WHAT HAPPENED
  The robot jumped 30cm forward the moment it was released at the start line. The controller had been accumulating error during the stall and released it all at once.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  While the robot was held at the start, the position error was large and constant, and the integrator summed it until the output hit the limit. The moment the hold released, the saturated output was applied instantly - a launch, not a start. Windup storage is invisible until the constraint disappears, which is why it always surfaces at the worst moment.
INVESTIGATION (before the fix)
  - Logged the integral term during the stall - it grew linearly
  - Confirmed the jump magnitude matched the stored integral
  - Added integral clamping and a pre-start integral reset
FIX (took 2 days)
  Fixed by clamping the integral to the output limits and resetting it when the robot is in the hold state, so the launch is a ramp, not a step.

E0694 | v6.7 | BIG | Found Day 116 | Fixed in 3 days | Pi SSH terminal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v6.7/spline_visualize.py
Error     : Global planner returns a path through the pillar
Terminal  : Pi SSH terminal
  $ python3 spline_visualize.py
  path waypoint 3: inside the pillar
  collision on the replay
WHAT HAPPENED
  The global planner produced a path that ran straight through a pillar. The replay showed the collision clearly - the planner never considered the robot's width.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The grid cost map marked only the obstacle's exact cells as blocked. A robot has physical width, so its center can be up to half a width away from an obstacle while the robot still collides. The planner used a point model for a 20cm-wide robot. Path planning for a real robot requires the configuration-space inflation; planning a point path through the environment is planning a point's path.
INVESTIGATION (before the fix)
  - Replayed the planned path against the map - the waypoint was inside
  - Measured the clearance at the collision - less than the robot width
  - Inflated the obstacles by the robot radius and re-planned
FIX (took 3 days)
  Fixed by inflating all obstacles by the robot radius before running A*, and adding a clearance check on the final path.

E0695 | v6.7 | BIG | Found Day 116 | Fixed in 4 days | Pi SSH terminal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v6.7/cubic_spline.py
Error     : Velocity profile ignores the corner limit
Terminal  : Pi SSH terminal
  $ python3 cubic_spline.py
  v = 2.0 m/s into a 60-degree corner
  tire squeal, robot drifts
WHAT HAPPENED
  The robot entered a 60-degree corner at full speed and slid wide. The profile optimized for time with no regard for what the tires can do.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The velocity profile minimized lap time subject only to acceleration limits, not to lateral acceleration. A corner has a speed limit set by physics: v_max = sqrt(mu * g * r). Ignoring the curvature limit produced a profile that is fast on paper and impossible in reality - the tires physically cannot provide the required lateral force.
INVESTIGATION (before the fix)
  - Measured the actual cornering speed limit on the track
  - Overlaid the profile's speed at the corner - it exceeded the limit
  - Added a curvature-dependent speed cap to the profile
FIX (took 4 days)
  Fixed by adding a speed cap derived from the path curvature and the measured tire limit, applied at every point of the profile.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
E0696 | v6.7 | BIG | Found Day 116 | Fixed in 5 days | Pi SSH terminal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v6.7/spline_visualize.py
Error     : Cubic spline path is jerky at waypoint 5
Terminal  : Pi SSH terminal
  $ python3 spline_visualize.py
  acceleration spike: 12 m/s^2 at wp5
  visible jerk in the run
WHAT HAPPENED
  At waypoint 5 the robot jerked visibly. The path was smooth to the eye - the jerk was in the timing, not the shape.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The spline was parameterized by a non-arc-length parameter, so equal parameter steps cover unequal distances along the path. The velocity controller interpreted parameter speed as spatial speed, producing huge accelerations where the parameterization compressed distance. A geometrically smooth path can be dynamically jerky if the parameterization is uneven.
INVESTIGATION (before the fix)
  - Plotted the path speed against distance - the spike matched wp5
  - Checked the parameterization - it was not arc length
  - Reparameterized by arc length and re-ran
FIX (took 5 days)
  Fixed by reparameterizing the spline with arc length so parameter speed equals spatial speed, and validating the acceleration profile in the profile_test.

E0697 | v6.8 | SMALL | Found Day 117 | Fixed in 1 day | systemd journal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v6.8/profile_test.py
Error     : Gain schedule jumps at the speed boundary
Terminal  : systemd journal
  $ python3 profile_test.py
  gain: 0.9 -> 2.4 (speed 1.00 m/s)
  steering step visible in the log
WHAT HAPPENED
  The steering gain jumped from 0.9 to 2.4 the instant the robot crossed 1 m/s. The steering response suddenly felt twice as aggressive.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The gain schedule was a lookup table with discrete rows, and the lookup switched rows at the boundary instead of interpolating between them. A discontinuous gain produces a discontinuous control law: the controller's personality changes instantly at a speed threshold. Gain scheduling is only smooth when the schedule itself is smooth.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by linearly interpolating between table rows, and adding a test that verifies the gain never changes by more than 10% per control tick.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
E0698 | v6.8 | SMALL | Found Day 117 | Fixed in 1 day | systemd journal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v6.8/velocity_profile.py
Error     : Feedforward sign is opposite on reverse
Terminal  : systemd journal
  $ python3 velocity_profile.py
  reverse + feedforward = wrong direction
  robot pulls to the left in reverse
WHAT HAPPENED
  In reverse, the robot consistently pulled to the left. The feedback controller was compensating correctly - the feedforward term was actively fighting it.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The feedforward steering term was computed for forward motion and applied unchanged when reversing. Steering geometry is direction-dependent: the same curvature requires the opposite steer correction when the velocity is negative. The sign flip was known in the ackermann module but not propagated to the controller, so two modules disagreed about the direction convention.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by multiplying the feedforward term by the direction sign, and adding a reverse-path test case to the controller test suite.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
E0699 | v6.8 | SMALL | Found Day 117 | Fixed in 1 day | systemd journal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v6.8/profile_test.py
Error     : Cubic spline overshoots past the goal
Terminal  : systemd journal
  $ python3 profile_test.py
  end: x=2.01 y=0.03 (goal 2.00, 0.00)
  overshoot 1cm at the parking spot
WHAT HAPPENED
  The spline ended 1cm past the parking target. Small in absolute terms, fatal for a parking maneuver where the tolerance is measured in millimeters.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The smoothing pass relaxed the endpoint constraints, letting the spline drift off the fixed end point. Splines are defined by their boundary conditions; the endpoint condition was applied before smoothing and the smoother was allowed to move it. The constraint was lost in the pipeline, not in the math.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by re-imposing the fixed endpoint condition after smoothing and adding a unit test that pins both endpoints to the exact goal.

E0704 | v6.8 | SMALL | Found Day 117 | Fixed in 1 day | systemd journal

File      : history/v6.8/velocity_profile.py
Error     : Stanley cross-track error is NaN at waypoint 0
Terminal  : systemd journal
  $ python3 velocity_profile.py
  cross_track: nan  (first waypoint)
  no steering command sent
WHAT HAPPENED
  The Stanley controller produced no steering command at the first waypoint. The cross-track error was NaN, so the controller output was NaN, and the car drove straight past the path.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The first path segment had zero length - two identical waypoints at the start of the list - so the tangent direction was undefined, and the cross-track math divided by zero. Stanley's formula assumes a valid segment direction; a zero-length segment violates that invariant. The NaN then propagated through the control output because no validation existed between the path math and the steering command.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by skipping zero-length segments in the path parser and replacing any NaN cross-track value with the previous valid value.

E0708 | v6.8 | BIG | Found Day 118 | Fixed in 5 days | Pi SSH terminal

File      : history/v6.8/velocity_profile.py
Error     : Feedforward causes overshoot in sharp turns
Terminal  : Pi SSH terminal
  $ python3 velocity_profile.py
  ff: +0.8 -> overshoot 8 degrees
  corrective jerk after each corner
WHAT HAPPENED
  After every sharp corner the robot overshot the heading by 8 degrees and then corrected with a jerk. Gentle corners were fine - only the sharp ones overshot.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The feedforward gain was tuned for the average curve and over-applied on sharp ones. The steering response is nonlinear: at large angles the servo linkage has different leverage, so a feedforward command calibrated for 30 degrees is too strong at 90. A single constant gain cannot fit a nonlinear plant across the whole operating range.
INVESTIGATION (before the fix)
  - Measured the overshoot against corner sharpness - it scaled with angle
  - Plotted the steer response vs command - nonlinear above 45 degrees
  - Scaled the feedforward with the corner curvature
FIX (took 5 days)
  Fixed by scaling the feedforward with the path curvature, and verifying with the corner_test that the overshoot stays under 2 degrees.

  The robot entered a 60-degree corner at full speed and slid wide. The profile optimized for time with no regard for what the tires can do.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The velocity profile minimized lap time subject only to acceleration limits, not to lateral acceleration. A corner has a speed limit set by physics: v_max = sqrt(mu * g * r). Ignoring the curvature limit produced a profile that is fast on paper and impossible in reality - the tires physically cannot provide the required lateral force.
INVESTIGATION (before the fix)
  - Measured the actual cornering speed limit on the track
  - Overlaid the profile's speed at the corner - it exceeded the limit
  - Added a curvature-dependent speed cap to the profile
FIX (took 2 days)
  Fixed by adding a speed cap derived from the path curvature and the measured tire limit, applied at every point of the profile.

E0718 | v6.9 | BIG | Found Day 120 | Fixed in 3 days | Pi SSH terminal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v6.9/obstacle_avoid.py
Error     : Cubic spline path is jerky at waypoint 5
Terminal  : Pi SSH terminal
  $ python3 obstacle_avoid.py
  acceleration spike: 12 m/s^2 at wp5
  visible jerk in the run
WHAT HAPPENED
  At waypoint 5 the robot jerked visibly. The path was smooth to the eye - the jerk was in the timing, not the shape.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The spline was parameterized by a non-arc-length parameter, so equal parameter steps cover unequal distances along the path. The velocity controller interpreted parameter speed as spatial speed, producing huge accelerations where the parameterization compressed distance. A geometrically smooth path can be dynamically jerky if the parameterization is uneven.
INVESTIGATION (before the fix)
  - Plotted the path speed against distance - the spike matched wp5
  - Checked the parameterization - it was not arc length
  - Reparameterized by arc length and re-ran
FIX (took 3 days)
  Fixed by reparameterizing the spline with arc length so parameter speed equals spatial speed, and validating the acceleration profile in the profile_test.

E0719 | v6.9 | BIG | Found Day 120 | Fixed in 4 days | Pi SSH terminal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v6.9/avoidance_test.py
Error     : Feedforward causes overshoot in sharp turns
Terminal  : Pi SSH terminal
  $ python3 avoidance_test.py
  ff: +0.8 -> overshoot 8 degrees
  corrective jerk after each corner
WHAT HAPPENED
  After every sharp corner the robot overshot the heading by 8 degrees and then corrected with a jerk. Gentle corners were fine - only the sharp ones overshot.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The feedforward gain was tuned for the average curve and over-applied on sharp ones. The steering response is nonlinear: at large angles the servo linkage has different leverage, so a feedforward command calibrated for 30 degrees is too strong at 90. A single constant gain cannot fit a nonlinear plant across the whole operating range.
INVESTIGATION (before the fix)
  - Measured the overshoot against corner sharpness - it scaled with angle
  - Plotted the steer response vs command - nonlinear above 45 degrees
  - Scaled the feedforward with the corner curvature
FIX (took 4 days)
  Fixed by scaling the feedforward with the path curvature, and verifying with the corner_test that the overshoot stays under 2 degrees.

E0720 | v6.9 | BIG | Found Day 120 | Fixed in 5 days | Pi SSH terminal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v6.9/obstacle_avoid.py
Error     : Anti-windup test fails with 30% overshoot
Terminal  : Pi SSH terminal
  $ python3 obstacle_avoid.py
  overshoot: 30% (target <10%)
  anti-windup not active
WHAT HAPPENED
  The windup test measured 30% overshoot - three times the target. The anti-windup code existed, was enabled, and did nothing.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The saturation check inside the anti-windup compared the output against the wrong limits - the controller's nominal range instead of the physical PWM limits. The controller output could never exceed its nominal range, so the saturation detector never triggered, so the anti-windup was permanently inactive. The feature was dead code with its documentation claiming otherwise.
INVESTIGATION (before the fix)
  - Read the windup_test output - the saturation flag never fired
  - Compared the check limits with the real PWM limits - they differed
  - Fixed the limits and re-ran - overshoot dropped to 4%
FIX (took 5 days)
  Fixed by comparing against the physical PWM limits in the saturation check, and adding a test assertion that the anti-windup flag actually activates during a stall.

E0721 | v7.0 | SMALL | Found Day 121 | Fixed in 1 day | Pi SSH terminal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v7.0/test_state_machine.py
Error     : Parking overshoots the zone by 10cm
Terminal  : Pi SSH terminal
  $ python3 test_state_machine.py
  final offset: 0.10m  (limit 0.05m)
  partial points only
WHAT HAPPENED
  The parking maneuver stopped 10cm outside the zone - double the allowed tolerance. The robot lost 8 points to the overshoot.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The final correction used the same approach speed as the main run, and the correction controller could not react before the robot rolled through the boundary. Parking corrections operate in millimeters and need low speeds; at the run speed the controller latency alone consumed the tolerance. The speed schedule was one value for all phases, and the parking phase needed a different one.

E0722 | v7.0 | SMALL | Found Day 121 | Fixed in 1 day | Pi SSH terminal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v7.0/state_machine.py
Error     : Checkpoint is missed on the fast lap
Terminal  : Pi SSH terminal
  $ python3 state_machine.py
  checkpoint 2: MISSED
  shortcut not detected at speed
WHAT HAPPENED
  The robot passed through checkpoint 2 at speed and the system never noticed. On slow laps the checkpoint always registered - the miss was speed-dependent.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The checkpoint gate was checked at 10Hz, and at 2m/s the robot crossed the gate in 60ms - faster than the check period. The checker literally never observed the crossing; the event happened between samples. Periodic sampling can only detect events that last longer than the sample period.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by checking the gate every frame instead of every 100ms, and adding a position interpolation that detects gate crossings between frames.

E0723 | v7.0 | SMALL | Found Day 121 | Fixed in 1 day | Pi SSH terminal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v7.0/test_state_machine.py
Error     : Race strategy picks the slow lane
Terminal  : Pi SSH terminal
  $ python3 test_state_machine.py
  lane: outer (inner was free)
  lost 0.8s per lap
WHAT HAPPENED
  The race strategy chose the outer lane while the inner lane was clear, losing 0.8 seconds per lap. The choice was stable and consistent - and consistently wrong.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The lane score was computed once before the race and considered only static geometry. The inner lane's obstacle was gone by lap 2, but the score still penalized it. A decision based on stale information is not a strategy error - it is an information freshness error. The strategy answered the question 'which lane was best 2 minutes ago'.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by recomputing the lane score every lap from the live obstacle state, and logging the score so a wrong choice is visible in the log.

E0724 | v7.0 | SMALL | Found Day 121 | Fixed in 1 day | Pi SSH terminal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v7.0/state_machine.py
Error     : Reverse logic oscillates at the obstacle
Terminal  : Pi SSH terminal
  $ python3 state_machine.py
  forward reverse forward reverse ...
  robot stuck for 4s
WHAT HAPPENED
  The robot shuffled forward and backward in front of an obstacle for four seconds. Both directions were correct decisions - in isolation.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The obstacle strategy evaluated the escape direction every frame, and each frame the evaluation flipped: after reversing a bit, the sensor saw a path forward again, and vice versa. A controller without state memory will oscillate whenever the sensor feedback lags the actuator. The hysteresis that exists in wall-following was missing here.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by adding a minimum dwell time in each direction state (0.5s), so the strategy commits to a direction instead of re-deciding every frame.

E0725 | v7.0 | SMALL | Found Day 121 | Fixed in 1 day | Pi SSH terminal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v7.0/test_state_machine.py
Error     : State machine stuck in IDLE
Terminal  : Pi SSH terminal
  $ python3 test_state_machine.py
  state: IDLE (30s)
  start line never detected
WHAT HAPPENED
  The robot sat at the start line for 30 seconds and never launched. The start detector was reporting, but the state machine was not listening.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The state machine waited for an event named 'start_detected', but the start detector published 'start_found'. Two modules used different names for the same fact - a vocabulary mismatch, not a logic error. Event-driven systems fail silently when events are named inconsistently, because the missing event simply never arrives.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by aligning the event names through a shared event constants module, and adding a startup check that logs the events each task publishes.

E0726 | v7.0 | SMALL | Found Day 121 | Fixed in 1 day | Pi SSH terminal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v7.0/state_machine.py
Error     : Lap counter double counts a lap
Terminal  : Pi SSH terminal
  $ python3 state_machine.py
  laps: 0 1 2 3 3 4 (double count at 3)
  race finished a lap early
WHAT HAPPENED
  The lap counter logged lap 3 twice, so the robot believed the race ended one lap early. The count went 3, 3 - two events for one crossing.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The lap line check ran on every frame while the robot was on the line, and every frame produced a lap event. There was no state to remember that the line had already been crossed. A threshold crossing is a single event, but a per-frame comparison produces one event per frame - the missing piece is edge detection, not counting.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by adding a crossed flag that only resets after the robot leaves the line, so one crossing produces exactly one event.

E0727 | v7.0 | SMALL | Found Day 121 | Fixed in 1 day | Pi SSH terminal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v7.0/test_state_machine.py
Error     : Start detected on camera noise
Terminal  : Pi SSH terminal
  $ python3 test_state_machine.py
  start: DETECTED (t=0.2s)
  robot launches before the judge signal
WHAT HAPPENED
  The robot launched 0.2 seconds after boot - before the judge's signal. A dark frame edge had matched the start pattern.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The start detector was a single-frame pattern match, and a single noisy frame can contain anything. With no confirmation requirement, one false match was enough to launch. Detection systems that decide from one sample have the error rate of one sample; the fix is statistical, not algorithmic - require agreement across time.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by requiring three consecutive confirmed frames (over 60ms) before launching, and rejecting the first 500ms of camera frames after start.

E0728 | v7.0 | SMALL | Found Day 121 | Fixed in 1 day | Pi SSH terminal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v7.0/state_machine.py
Error     : Direction is inverted after the first reverse
Terminal  : Pi SSH terminal
  $ python3 state_machine.py
  direction: forward (robot is reversing)
  pillar logic wrong side
WHAT HAPPENED
  After the first reverse maneuver the robot's direction state said FORWARD while it was physically reversing. All pillar logic that depended on direction was wrong from that moment.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The reverse command was executed by the motor layer, but the direction flag lived in a different module and was never updated when the reverse command ran. Two copies of the truth (the actual motion and the recorded state) diverged, and nothing enforced their consistency. The state was updated at the command level, not at the motion level where the truth exists.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by updating the direction flag inside the reverse state action, and adding an assertion that compares the flag against the motor layer's reported direction.

Error     : Race strategy bets everything on the wrong lane
Terminal  : Pi SSH terminal
  $ python3 test_state_machine.py
  lane chosen: outer (inner clear)
  lost 1.5s over the race
WHAT HAPPENED
  The race strategy committed to the outer lane for all three laps while the inner lane was clear from lap 2 on. A wrong early decision was locked in.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The lane decision was made once before lap 1 from a single observation. Track conditions change during a race - an obstacle may move or a line may clear - and a one-time decision cannot adapt. Committing to a fixed plan in a dynamic environment turns every change into a penalty.

E0730 | v7.0 | BIG | Found Day 122 | Fixed in 3 days | Pi SSH terminal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v7.0/state_machine.py
Error     : Checkpoint gate triggers twice per crossing
Terminal  : Pi SSH terminal
  $ python3 state_machine.py
  checkpoint 3: 2 events
  bonus counted twice
WHAT HAPPENED
  Every checkpoint produced two events instead of one, doubling the bonus count. The scoring was quietly wrong by a factor of two.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The gate trigger fired on both the leading edge and the trailing edge of the crossing - the code treated entering and leaving the gate as two separate events. A gate is a region, and the trigger logic did not define which transition counts. Without an explicit edge definition, every boundary transition is an event.
INVESTIGATION (before the fix)
  - Counted the events per crossing - exactly two, every time
  - Traced the trigger to both boundary transitions
  - Added a cleared-edge requirement and re-ran
FIX (took 3 days)
  Fixed by triggering only on entry and requiring the gate to be fully cleared before the next trigger, verified in the checkpoint test.

E0731 | v7.0 | BIG | Found Day 122 | Fixed in 4 days | Pi SSH terminal

File      : history/v7.0/test_state_machine.py
Error     : Reverse logic stalls at a wall
Terminal  : Pi SSH terminal
  $ python3 test_state_machine.py
  reverse: 0.2s, forward: 0.2s, loop
  robot stuck for 9s
WHAT HAPPENED
  The robot shuffled against a wall for nine seconds, reversing 0.2s and advancing 0.2s forever. Both motions worked; the combination was useless.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The reverse duration was a fixed 0.2 seconds, shorter than the time needed to clear the wall overlap. A fixed parameter can only be correct for one geometry; the wall overlap varies.
INVESTIGATION (before the fix)

  - Timed how long a reverse needed to clear the overlap
  - Made the reverse distance proportional to the overlap
FIX (took 4 days)

E0732 | v7.0 | BIG | Found Day 122 | Fixed in 5 days | Pi SSH terminal

  $ python3 state_machine.py
  laps: 2 (stopped exactly on the line)
  race cannot finish
WHAT HAPPENED
  The robot stopped exactly on the lap line and the counter refused to advance. The robot was on the line - why did the count not register?

Error     : Race strategy picks the slow lane
Terminal  : ESP32 serial monitor
  $ python3 lap_counter.py
  lane: outer (inner was free)
  lost 0.8s per lap
WHAT HAPPENED
  The race strategy chose the outer lane while the inner lane was clear, losing 0.8 seconds per lap. The choice was stable and consistent - and consistently wrong.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The lane score was computed once before the race and considered only static geometry. The inner lane's obstacle was gone by lap 2, but the score still penalized it. A decision based on stale information is not a strategy error - it is an information freshness error. The strategy answered the question 'which lane was best 2 minutes ago'.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by recomputing the lane score every lap from the live obstacle state, and logging the score so a wrong choice is visible in the log.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
E0746 | v7.2 | SMALL | Found Day 125 | Fixed in 1 day | ESP32 serial monitor
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v7.2/test_lap_counter.py
Error     : Reverse logic oscillates at the obstacle
Terminal  : ESP32 serial monitor
  $ python3 test_lap_counter.py
  forward reverse forward reverse ...
  robot stuck for 4s
WHAT HAPPENED
  The robot shuffled forward and backward in front of an obstacle for four seconds. Both directions were correct decisions - in isolation.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The obstacle strategy evaluated the escape direction every frame, and each frame the evaluation flipped: after reversing a bit, the sensor saw a path forward again, and vice versa. A controller without state memory will oscillate whenever the sensor feedback lags the actuator. The hysteresis that exists in wall-following was missing here.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by adding a minimum dwell time in each direction state (0.5s), so the strategy commits to a direction instead of re-deciding every frame.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
E0747 | v7.2 | SMALL | Found Day 125 | Fixed in 1 day | ESP32 serial monitor
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v7.2/lap_counter.py
Error     : State machine stuck in IDLE
Terminal  : ESP32 serial monitor
  $ python3 lap_counter.py
  state: IDLE (30s)
  start line never detected
WHAT HAPPENED
  The robot sat at the start line for 30 seconds and never launched. The start detector was reporting, but the state machine was not listening.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The state machine waited for an event named 'start_detected', but the start detector published 'start_found'. Two modules used different names for the same fact - a vocabulary mismatch, not a logic error. Event-driven systems fail silently when events are named inconsistently, because the missing event simply never arrives.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by aligning the event names through a shared event constants module, and adding a startup check that logs the events each task publishes.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
E0748 | v7.2 | SMALL | Found Day 125 | Fixed in 1 day | ESP32 serial monitor
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v7.2/test_lap_counter.py
Error     : Lap counter double counts a lap
Terminal  : ESP32 serial monitor
  $ python3 test_lap_counter.py
  laps: 0 1 2 3 3 4 (double count at 3)
  race finished a lap early
WHAT HAPPENED
  The lap counter logged lap 3 twice, so the robot believed the race ended one lap early. The count went 3, 3 - two events for one crossing.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The lap line check ran on every frame while the robot was on the line, and every frame produced a lap event. There was no state to remember that the line had already been crossed. A threshold crossing is a single event, but a per-frame comparison produces one event per frame - the missing piece is edge detection, not counting.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by adding a crossed flag that only resets after the robot leaves the line, so one crossing produces exactly one event.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
E0749 | v7.2 | SMALL | Found Day 125 | Fixed in 1 day | ESP32 serial monitor
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v7.2/lap_counter.py
Error     : Start detected on camera noise
Terminal  : ESP32 serial monitor
  $ python3 lap_counter.py
  start: DETECTED (t=0.2s)
  robot launches before the judge signal
WHAT HAPPENED
  The robot launched 0.2 seconds after boot - before the judge's signal. A dark frame edge had matched the start pattern.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The start detector was a single-frame pattern match, and a single noisy frame can contain anything. With no confirmation requirement, one false match was enough to launch. Detection systems that decide from one sample have the error rate of one sample; the fix is statistical, not algorithmic - require agreement across time.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by requiring three consecutive confirmed frames (over 60ms) before launching, and rejecting the first 500ms of camera frames after start.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
E0750 | v7.2 | SMALL | Found Day 125 | Fixed in 1 day | ESP32 serial monitor
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v7.2/test_lap_counter.py
Error     : Direction is inverted after the first reverse
Terminal  : ESP32 serial monitor
  $ python3 test_lap_counter.py
  direction: forward (robot is reversing)
  pillar logic wrong side
WHAT HAPPENED
  After the first reverse maneuver the robot's direction state said FORWARD while it was physically reversing. All pillar logic that depended on direction was wrong from that moment.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The reverse command was executed by the motor layer, but the direction flag lived in a different module and was never updated when the reverse command ran. Two copies of the truth (the actual motion and the recorded state) diverged, and nothing enforced their consistency. The state was updated at the command level, not at the motion level where the truth exists.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by updating the direction flag inside the reverse state action, and adding an assertion that compares the flag against the motor layer's reported direction.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
E0751 | v7.2 | SMALL | Found Day 125 | Fixed in 1 day | ESP32 serial monitor
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v7.2/lap_counter.py
Error     : Parking overshoots the zone by 10cm
Terminal  : ESP32 serial monitor
  $ python3 lap_counter.py
  final offset: 0.10m  (limit 0.05m)
  partial points only
WHAT HAPPENED
  The parking maneuver stopped 10cm outside the zone - double the allowed tolerance. The robot lost 8 points to the overshoot.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The final correction used the same approach speed as the main run, and the correction controller could not react before the robot rolled through the boundary. Parking corrections operate in millimeters and need low speeds; at the run speed the controller latency alone consumed the tolerance. The speed schedule was one value for all phases, and the parking phase needed a different one.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by switching to CRAB_WALK for the last 10cm and capping the park approach speed at 0.15 m/s, with the tolerance margin verified in the park_sm test.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
E0752 | v7.2 | SMALL | Found Day 125 | Fixed in 1 day | ESP32 serial monitor
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v7.2/test_lap_counter.py
Error     : Checkpoint is missed on the fast lap
Terminal  : ESP32 serial monitor
  $ python3 test_lap_counter.py
  checkpoint 2: MISSED
  shortcut not detected at speed
WHAT HAPPENED
  The robot passed through checkpoint 2 at speed and the system never noticed. On slow laps the checkpoint always registered - the miss was speed-dependent.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The checkpoint gate was checked at 10Hz, and at 2m/s the robot crossed the gate in 60ms - faster than the check period. The checker literally never observed the crossing; the event happened between samples. Periodic sampling can only detect events that last longer than the sample period.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by checking the gate every frame instead of every 100ms, and adding a position interpolation that detects gate crossings between frames.

E0753 | v7.2 | BIG | Found Day 126 | Fixed in 2 days | Pi SSH terminal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v7.2/lap_counter.py
Error     : Reverse logic stalls at a wall
Terminal  : Pi SSH terminal
  $ python3 lap_counter.py
  reverse: 0.2s, forward: 0.2s, loop
  robot stuck for 9s
WHAT HAPPENED
  The robot shuffled against a wall for nine seconds, reversing 0.2s and advancing 0.2s forever. Both motions worked; the combination was useless.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The reverse duration was a fixed 0.2 seconds, shorter than the time needed to clear the wall overlap. Each forward attempt re-engaged the wall by more than the reverse had cleared, so the net progress per cycle was negative. A fixed parameter can only be correct for one geometry; the wall overlap varies.
INVESTIGATION (before the fix)
  - Measured the wall overlap vs the reverse distance - negative net
  - Timed how long a reverse needed to clear the overlap
  - Made the reverse distance proportional to the overlap
FIX (took 2 days)
  Fixed by making the reverse distance proportional to the measured obstacle overlap, and adding a minimum total reverse time to the strategy.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
E0754 | v7.2 | BIG | Found Day 126 | Fixed in 3 days | Pi SSH terminal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v7.2/test_lap_counter.py
Error     : Lap counter breaks when the robot stops on the line
Terminal  : Pi SSH terminal
  $ python3 test_lap_counter.py
  laps: 2 (stopped exactly on the line)
  race cannot finish
WHAT HAPPENED
  The robot stopped exactly on the lap line and the counter refused to advance. The robot was on the line - why did the count not register?
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The lap counter only counted a lap when it observed a transition from 'not on line' to 'on line'. The robot crossed the line while the counter was still resolving the previous state, so no transition was ever observed. Counting transitions instead of positions means a valid crossing can be invisible if it coincides with the state resolution.
INVESTIGATION (before the fix)
  - Reproduced by stopping exactly on the line
  - Checked the counter logic - it demanded a transition
  - Added a position-based check that accepts a stationary crossing
FIX (took 3 days)
  Fixed by also counting a lap when the robot is detected on the line in the correct direction while the previous lap is already confirmed.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
E0755 | v7.2 | BIG | Found Day 126 | Fixed in 4 days | Pi SSH terminal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v7.2/lap_counter.py
Error     : State machine enters PARK during lap 2
Terminal  : Pi SSH terminal
  $ python3 lap_counter.py
  state: PARK (lap 2 of 3)
  lap counter said 3/3
WHAT HAPPENED
  The robot parked after lap 2 of 3 because the lap counter believed the race was over. The count was wrong - the state machine trusted it.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  A bump at the line made the lap counter double-count, and the race strategy terminates when laps reach 3. The state machine faithfully executed its instructions; the instructions were based on corrupted data. Two subsystems were coupled through a counter with no validation, so an error in one silently propagated to the other.
INVESTIGATION (before the fix)
  - Replayed the bump - it produced two lap events
  - Confirmed the state machine acted on the wrong count
  - Fixed the counter with edge detection, then verified the full race
FIX (took 4 days)
  Fixed by requiring a full line crossing with cleared-edge detection to count a lap, and adding a sanity check that rejects lap counts closer than 3 seconds apart.

E0756 | v7.2 | BIG | Found Day 126 | Fixed in 5 days | Pi SSH terminal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v7.2/test_lap_counter.py
Error     : Start line missed because the camera was still warming
Terminal  : Pi SSH terminal
  $ python3 test_lap_counter.py
  start: never detected (60s)
  camera ready at t=8s, start at t=3s
WHAT HAPPENED
  The robot missed the start line entirely because the camera was not ready when the line appeared. The detector ran blind and nobody knew.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The start detector subscribed to camera frames the moment the pipeline started, but the camera needed 8 seconds to produce usable frames. The start line was crossed at t=3s - before the first good frame. The detector reported 'no line' for frames that did not exist; there was no readiness signal between the camera and the detector.
INVESTIGATION (before the fix)
  - Timed the camera readiness - 8s, longer than the approach
  - Logged the frames the detector actually saw - zero valid ones
  - Added a camera-ready signal gating the start detection
FIX (took 5 days)
  Fixed by delaying the start detection until the camera reports ready, and logging 'camera warming' during the wait so the state is visible.

  Fixed by switching to CRAB_WALK for the last 10cm and capping the park approach speed at 0.15 m/s, with the tolerance margin verified in the park_sm test.

E0774 | v7.4 | SMALL | Found Day 129 | Fixed in 1 day | systemd journal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v7.4/test_obstacle_strategy.py
Error     : Checkpoint is missed on the fast lap
Terminal  : systemd journal
  $ python3 test_obstacle_strategy.py
  checkpoint 2: MISSED
  shortcut not detected at speed
WHAT HAPPENED
  The robot passed through checkpoint 2 at speed and the system never noticed. On slow laps the checkpoint always registered - the miss was speed-dependent.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The checkpoint gate was checked at 10Hz, and at 2m/s the robot crossed the gate in 60ms - faster than the check period. The checker literally never observed the crossing; the event happened between samples. Periodic sampling can only detect events that last longer than the sample period.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by checking the gate every frame instead of every 100ms, and adding a position interpolation that detects gate crossings between frames.

E0775 | v7.4 | SMALL | Found Day 129 | Fixed in 1 day | systemd journal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v7.4/obstacle_strategy.py
Error     : Race strategy picks the slow lane
Terminal  : systemd journal
  $ python3 obstacle_strategy.py
  lane: outer (inner was free)
  lost 0.8s per lap
WHAT HAPPENED
  The race strategy chose the outer lane while the inner lane was clear, losing 0.8 seconds per lap. The choice was stable and consistent - and consistently wrong.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The lane score was computed once before the race and considered only static geometry. The inner lane's obstacle was gone by lap 2, but the score still penalized it. A decision based on stale information is not a strategy error - it is an information freshness error. The strategy answered the question 'which lane was best 2 minutes ago'.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by recomputing the lane score every lap from the live obstacle state, and logging the score so a wrong choice is visible in the log.

E0776 | v7.4 | SMALL | Found Day 129 | Fixed in 1 day | systemd journal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v7.4/test_obstacle_strategy.py
Error     : Reverse logic oscillates at the obstacle
Terminal  : systemd journal
  $ python3 test_obstacle_strategy.py
  forward reverse forward reverse ...
  robot stuck for 4s
WHAT HAPPENED
  The robot shuffled forward and backward in front of an obstacle for four seconds. Both directions were correct decisions - in isolation.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The obstacle strategy evaluated the escape direction every frame, and each frame the evaluation flipped: after reversing a bit, the sensor saw a path forward again, and vice versa. A controller without state memory will oscillate whenever the sensor feedback lags the actuator. The hysteresis that exists in wall-following was missing here.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by adding a minimum dwell time in each direction state (0.5s), so the strategy commits to a direction instead of re-deciding every frame.

E0777 | v7.4 | BIG | Found Day 130 | Fixed in 2 days | Pi SSH terminal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v7.4/obstacle_strategy.py
Error     : State machine enters PARK during lap 2
Terminal  : Pi SSH terminal
  $ python3 obstacle_strategy.py
  state: PARK (lap 2 of 3)
  lap counter said 3/3
WHAT HAPPENED
  The robot parked after lap 2 of 3 because the lap counter believed the race was over. The count was wrong - the state machine trusted it.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  A bump at the line made the lap counter double-count, and the race strategy terminates when laps reach 3. The state machine faithfully executed its instructions; the instructions were based on corrupted data. Two subsystems were coupled through a counter with no validation, so an error in one silently propagated to the other.
INVESTIGATION (before the fix)
  - Replayed the bump - it produced two lap events
  - Confirmed the state machine acted on the wrong count
  - Fixed the counter with edge detection, then verified the full race
FIX (took 2 days)
  Fixed by requiring a full line crossing with cleared-edge detection to count a lap, and adding a sanity check that rejects lap counts closer than 3 seconds apart.

E0778 | v7.4 | BIG | Found Day 130 | Fixed in 3 days | Pi SSH terminal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v7.4/test_obstacle_strategy.py
Error     : Start line missed because the camera was still warming
Terminal  : Pi SSH terminal
  $ python3 test_obstacle_strategy.py
  start: never detected (60s)
  camera ready at t=8s, start at t=3s
WHAT HAPPENED
  The robot missed the start line entirely because the camera was not ready when the line appeared. The detector ran blind and nobody knew.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The start detector subscribed to camera frames the moment the pipeline started, but the camera needed 8 seconds to produce usable frames. The start line was crossed at t=3s - before the first good frame. The detector reported 'no line' for frames that did not exist; there was no readiness signal between the camera and the detector.
INVESTIGATION (before the fix)
  - Timed the camera readiness - 8s, longer than the approach
  - Logged the frames the detector actually saw - zero valid ones
  - Added a camera-ready signal gating the start detection
FIX (took 3 days)
  Fixed by delaying the start detection until the camera reports ready, and logging 'camera warming' during the wait so the state is visible.

E0779 | v7.4 | BIG | Found Day 130 | Fixed in 4 days | Pi SSH terminal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v7.4/obstacle_strategy.py
Error     : Direction logic fails after a 180-degree obstacle
Terminal  : Pi SSH terminal
  $ python3 obstacle_strategy.py
  direction: forward (robot now reversed)
  pillars tracked on the wrong side
WHAT HAPPENED
  After a 180-degree avoidance maneuver the robot tracked pillars on the wrong side. The direction state still said forward while the robot faced backward.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The 180-degree maneuver was implemented in the obstacle strategy as a series of motor commands, bypassing the normal direction-tracking code path. The direction module had no knowledge of the maneuver, so its state was stale. When the logic is bypassed, the state that depends on it silently rots.
INVESTIGATION (before the fix)
  - Replayed the maneuver - the flag never changed
  - Found the bypass in the obstacle strategy code
  - Routed the maneuver through the direction module
FIX (took 4 days)
  Fixed by implementing the 180-degree maneuver inside the direction module, and adding an assertion that the direction flag matches the IMU heading within 30 degrees.

E0780 | v7.4 | BIG | Found Day 130 | Fixed in 5 days | Pi SSH terminal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v7.4/test_obstacle_strategy.py
Error     : Parking state overshoots and hits the wall
Terminal  : Pi SSH terminal
  $ python3 test_obstacle_strategy.py
  park: robot 12cm past the line
  wall bump at 0.4m/s
WHAT HAPPENED
  The parking maneuver drove 12cm past the line and bumped the wall at 0.4 m/s. The park logic was correct - the speed was not.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The park state reused the race approach speed of 0.4 m/s. At that speed the robot travels 40cm in one second, and the parking correction latency is several hundred milliseconds - the stopping distance alone exceeded the zone tolerance. Parking is a precision task executed with race parameters.
INVESTIGATION (before the fix)
  - Measured the stopping distance at the park speed - over the tolerance
  - Checked the park approach speed - it was the race value
  - Capped the park speed and re-ran the park_sm test
FIX (took 5 days)
  Fixed by capping the park approach speed at 0.15 m/s and adding a distance budget check that aborts the approach if the remaining distance is insufficient to stop.

E0781 | v7.5 | SMALL | Found Day 131 | Fixed in 1 day | VS Code terminal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v7.5/direction_detect.py
Error     : Lap counter double counts a lap
Terminal  : VS Code terminal
  $ python3 direction_detect.py
  laps: 0 1 2 3 3 4 (double count at 3)
  race finished a lap early
WHAT HAPPENED
  The lap counter logged lap 3 twice, so the robot believed the race ended one lap early. The count went 3, 3 - two events for one crossing.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The lap line check ran on every frame while the robot was on the line, and every frame produced a lap event. There was no state to remember that the line had already been crossed. A threshold crossing is a single event, but a per-frame comparison produces one event per frame - the missing piece is edge detection, not counting.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by adding a crossed flag that only resets after the robot leaves the line, so one crossing produces exactly one event.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
E0782 | v7.5 | SMALL | Found Day 131 | Fixed in 1 day | VS Code terminal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v7.5/test_direction_detect.py
Error     : Start detected on camera noise
Terminal  : VS Code terminal
  $ python3 test_direction_detect.py
  start: DETECTED (t=0.2s)
  robot launches before the judge signal
WHAT HAPPENED
  The robot launched 0.2 seconds after boot - before the judge's signal. A dark frame edge had matched the start pattern.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The start detector was a single-frame pattern match, and a single noisy frame can contain anything. With no confirmation requirement, one false match was enough to launch. Detection systems that decide from one sample have the error rate of one sample; the fix is statistical, not algorithmic - require agreement across time.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by requiring three consecutive confirmed frames (over 60ms) before launching, and rejecting the first 500ms of camera frames after start.

E0783 | v7.5 | SMALL | Found Day 131 | Fixed in 1 day | VS Code terminal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v7.5/direction_detect.py
Error     : Direction is inverted after the first reverse
Terminal  : VS Code terminal
  $ python3 direction_detect.py
  direction: forward (robot is reversing)
  pillar logic wrong side
WHAT HAPPENED
  After the first reverse maneuver the robot's direction state said FORWARD while it was physically reversing. All pillar logic that depended on direction was wrong from that moment.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The reverse command was executed by the motor layer, but the direction flag lived in a different module and was never updated when the reverse command ran. Two copies of the truth (the actual motion and the recorded state) diverged, and nothing enforced their consistency. The state was updated at the command level, not at the motion level where the truth exists.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by updating the direction flag inside the reverse state action, and adding an assertion that compares the flag against the motor layer's reported direction.

E0784 | v7.5 | SMALL | Found Day 131 | Fixed in 1 day | VS Code terminal

Error     : Parking overshoots the zone by 10cm
Terminal  : VS Code terminal
  $ python3 test_direction_detect.py
  final offset: 0.10m  (limit 0.05m)
  partial points only
WHAT HAPPENED
  The parking maneuver stopped 10cm outside the zone - double the allowed tolerance. The robot lost 8 points to the overshoot.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The final correction used the same approach speed as the main run, and the correction controller could not react before the robot rolled through the boundary. Parking corrections operate in millimeters and need low speeds; at the run speed the controller latency alone consumed the tolerance. The speed schedule was one value for all phases, and the parking phase needed a different one.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by switching to CRAB_WALK for the last 10cm and capping the park approach speed at 0.15 m/s, with the tolerance margin verified in the park_sm test.

  state: IDLE (30s)
  start line never detected
WHAT HAPPENED
  The robot sat at the start line for 30 seconds and never launched. The start detector was reporting, but the state machine was not listening.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)

  park: robot 12cm past the line
  wall bump at 0.4m/s
WHAT HAPPENED
  The parking maneuver drove 12cm past the line and bumped the wall at 0.4 m/s. The park logic was correct - the speed was not.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The park state reused the race approach speed of 0.4 m/s. At that speed the robot travels 40cm in one second, and the parking correction latency is several hundred milliseconds - the stopping distance alone exceeded the zone tolerance. Parking is a precision task executed with race parameters.
INVESTIGATION (before the fix)
  - Measured the stopping distance at the park speed - over the tolerance
  - Checked the park approach speed - it was the race value
  - Capped the park speed and re-ran the park_sm test
FIX (took 3 days)
  Fixed by capping the park approach speed at 0.15 m/s and adding a distance budget check that aborts the approach if the remaining distance is insufficient to stop.

E0804 | v7.6 | BIG | Found Day 134 | Fixed in 5 days | Pi SSH terminal
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v7.6/test_reverse_logic.py
Error     : Checkpoint gate triggers twice per crossing
Terminal  : Pi SSH terminal
  $ python3 test_reverse_logic.py
  checkpoint 3: 2 events
  bonus counted twice
WHAT HAPPENED
  Every checkpoint produced two events instead of one, doubling the bonus count. The scoring was quietly wrong by a factor of two.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The gate trigger fired on both the leading edge and the trailing edge of the crossing - the code treated entering and leaving the gate as two separate events. A gate is a region, and the trigger logic did not define which transition counts. Without an explicit edge definition, every boundary transition is an event.
INVESTIGATION (before the fix)
  - Counted the events per crossing - exactly two, every time
  - Traced the trigger to both boundary transitions
  - Added a cleared-edge requirement and re-ran
FIX (took 5 days)
  Fixed by triggering only on entry and requiring the gate to be fully cleared before the next trigger, verified in the checkpoint test.

E0805 | v7.7 | SMALL | Found Day 135 | Fixed in 1 day | Pi console (HDMI)
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v7.7/park_sm.py
Error     : Direction is inverted after the first reverse
Terminal  : Pi console (HDMI)
  $ python3 park_sm.py
  direction: forward (robot is reversing)
  pillar logic wrong side
WHAT HAPPENED
  After the first reverse maneuver the robot's direction state said FORWARD while it was physically reversing. All pillar logic that depended on direction was wrong from that moment.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The reverse command was executed by the motor layer, but the direction flag lived in a different module and was never updated when the reverse command ran. Two copies of the truth (the actual motion and the recorded state) diverged, and nothing enforced their consistency. The state was updated at the command level, not at the motion level where the truth exists.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by updating the direction flag inside the reverse state action, and adding an assertion that compares the flag against the motor layer's reported direction.

E0806 | v7.7 | SMALL | Found Day 135 | Fixed in 1 day | Pi console (HDMI)
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v7.7/test_park_sm.py
Error     : Parking overshoots the zone by 10cm
Terminal  : Pi console (HDMI)
  $ python3 test_park_sm.py
  final offset: 0.10m  (limit 0.05m)
  partial points only
WHAT HAPPENED
  The parking maneuver stopped 10cm outside the zone - double the allowed tolerance. The robot lost 8 points to the overshoot.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The final correction used the same approach speed as the main run, and the correction controller could not react before the robot rolled through the boundary. Parking corrections operate in millimeters and need low speeds; at the run speed the controller latency alone consumed the tolerance. The speed schedule was one value for all phases, and the parking phase needed a different one.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by switching to CRAB_WALK for the last 10cm and capping the park approach speed at 0.15 m/s, with the tolerance margin verified in the park_sm test.

E0807 | v7.7 | SMALL | Found Day 135 | Fixed in 1 day | Pi console (HDMI)
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v7.7/park_sm.py
Error     : Checkpoint is missed on the fast lap
Terminal  : Pi console (HDMI)
  $ python3 park_sm.py
  checkpoint 2: MISSED
  shortcut not detected at speed
WHAT HAPPENED
  The robot passed through checkpoint 2 at speed and the system never noticed. On slow laps the checkpoint always registered - the miss was speed-dependent.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The checkpoint gate was checked at 10Hz, and at 2m/s the robot crossed the gate in 60ms - faster than the check period. The checker literally never observed the crossing; the event happened between samples. Periodic sampling can only detect events that last longer than the sample period.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by checking the gate every frame instead of every 100ms, and adding a position interpolation that detects gate crossings between frames.

E0808 | v7.7 | SMALL | Found Day 135 | Fixed in 1 day | Pi console (HDMI)
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v7.7/test_park_sm.py
Error     : Race strategy picks the slow lane
Terminal  : Pi console (HDMI)
  $ python3 test_park_sm.py
  lane: outer (inner was free)
  lost 0.8s per lap
WHAT HAPPENED
  The race strategy chose the outer lane while the inner lane was clear, losing 0.8 seconds per lap. The choice was stable and consistent - and consistently wrong.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The lane score was computed once before the race and considered only static geometry. The inner lane's obstacle was gone by lap 2, but the score still penalized it. A decision based on stale information is not a strategy error - it is an information freshness error. The strategy answered the question 'which lane was best 2 minutes ago'.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by recomputing the lane score every lap from the live obstacle state, and logging the score so a wrong choice is visible in the log.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
E0809 | v7.7 | SMALL | Found Day 135 | Fixed in 1 day | Pi console (HDMI)
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v7.7/park_sm.py
Error     : Reverse logic oscillates at the obstacle
Terminal  : Pi console (HDMI)
  $ python3 park_sm.py
  forward reverse forward reverse ...
  robot stuck for 4s
WHAT HAPPENED
  The robot shuffled forward and backward in front of an obstacle for four seconds. Both directions were correct decisions - in isolation.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The obstacle strategy evaluated the escape direction every frame, and each frame the evaluation flipped: after reversing a bit, the sensor saw a path forward again, and vice versa. A controller without state memory will oscillate whenever the sensor feedback lags the actuator. The hysteresis that exists in wall-following was missing here.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by adding a minimum dwell time in each direction state (0.5s), so the strategy commits to a direction instead of re-deciding every frame.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
E0810 | v7.7 | SMALL | Found Day 135 | Fixed in 1 day | Pi console (HDMI)
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v7.7/test_park_sm.py
Error     : State machine stuck in IDLE
Terminal  : Pi console (HDMI)
  $ python3 test_park_sm.py
  state: IDLE (30s)
  start line never detected
WHAT HAPPENED
  The robot sat at the start line for 30 seconds and never launched. The start detector was reporting, but the state machine was not listening.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The state machine waited for an event named 'start_detected', but the start detector published 'start_found'. Two modules used different names for the same fact - a vocabulary mismatch, not a logic error. Event-driven systems fail silently when events are named inconsistently, because the missing event simply never arrives.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by aligning the event names through a shared event constants module, and adding a startup check that logs the events each task publishes.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
E0811 | v7.7 | SMALL | Found Day 135 | Fixed in 1 day | Pi console (HDMI)
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v7.7/park_sm.py
Error     : Lap counter double counts a lap
Terminal  : Pi console (HDMI)
  $ python3 park_sm.py
  laps: 0 1 2 3 3 4 (double count at 3)
  race finished a lap early
WHAT HAPPENED
  The lap counter logged lap 3 twice, so the robot believed the race ended one lap early. The count went 3, 3 - two events for one crossing.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The lap line check ran on every frame while the robot was on the line, and every frame produced a lap event. There was no state to remember that the line had already been crossed. A threshold crossing is a single event, but a per-frame comparison produces one event per frame - the missing piece is edge detection, not counting.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by adding a crossed flag that only resets after the robot leaves the line, so one crossing produces exactly one event.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
E0812 | v7.7 | SMALL | Found Day 135 | Fixed in 1 day | Pi console (HDMI)
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v7.7/test_park_sm.py
Error     : Start detected on camera noise
Terminal  : Pi console (HDMI)
  $ python3 test_park_sm.py
  start: DETECTED (t=0.2s)
  robot launches before the judge signal
WHAT HAPPENED
  The robot launched 0.2 seconds after boot - before the judge's signal. A dark frame edge had matched the start pattern.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The start detector was a single-frame pattern match, and a single noisy frame can contain anything. With no confirmation requirement, one false match was enough to launch. Detection systems that decide from one sample have the error rate of one sample; the fix is statistical, not algorithmic - require agreement across time.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by requiring three consecutive confirmed frames (over 60ms) before launching, and rejecting the first 500ms of camera frames after start.

Terminal  : Pi SSH terminal
  $ python3 test_park_sm.py

WHAT HAPPENED

  $ python3 test_race_strategy.py
  laps: 2 (stopped exactly on the line)
  race cannot finish
WHAT HAPPENED
  The robot stopped exactly on the lap line and the counter refused to advance. The robot was on the line - why did the count not register?
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)

  - Added a position-based check that accepts a stationary crossing

  The race strategy chose the outer lane while the inner lane was clear, losing 0.8 seconds per lap. The choice was stable and consistent - and consistently wrong.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The lane score was computed once before the race and considered only static geometry. The inner lane's obstacle was gone by lap 2, but the score still penalized it. A decision based on stale information is not a strategy error - it is an information freshness error. The strategy answered the question 'which lane was best 2 minutes ago'.
FIX (took 1 day)
  Fixed by recomputing the lane score every lap from the live obstacle state, and logging the score so a wrong choice is visible in the log.

E0831 | v7.9 | SMALL | Found Day 139 | Fixed in 1 day | Windows CMD
----------------------------------------------------------------------
File      : history/v7.9/checkpoint.py
Error     : Reverse logic oscillates at the obstacle
Terminal  : Windows CMD
  $ python3 checkpoint.py
  forward reverse forward reverse ...
  robot stuck for 4s
WHAT HAPPENED
  The robot shuffled forward and backward in front of an obstacle for four seconds. Both directions were correct decisions - in isolation.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The obstacle strategy evaluated the escape direction every frame, and each frame the evaluation flipped: after reversing a bit, the sensor saw a path forward again, and vice versa. A controller without state memory will oscillate whenever the sensor feedback lags the actuator. The hysteresis that exists in wall-following was missing here.
FIX (took 1 day)

E0832 | v7.9 | SMALL | Found Day 139 | Fixed in 1 day | Windows CMD

Terminal  : Windows CMD
  $ python3 test_checkpoint.py
  state: IDLE (30s)
  start line never detected
WHAT HAPPENED
  The robot sat at the start line for 30 seconds and never launched. The start detector was reporting, but the state machine was not listening.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The state machine waited for an event named 'start_detected', but the start detector published 'start_found'. WHAT HAPPENED
  The lap counter logged lap 3 twice, so the robot believed the race ended one lap early. The count went 3, 3 - two events for one crossing.

E0837 | v7.9 | BIG | Found Day 140 | Fixed in 2 days | Pi SSH terminal

File      : history/v7.9/checkpoint.py
Error     : Checkpoint gate triggers twice per crossing
Terminal  : Pi SSH terminal
  $ python3 checkpoint.py
  checkpoint 3: 2 events
  bonus counted twice
WHAT HAPPENED
  Every checkpoint produced two events instead of one, doubling the bonus count. The scoring was quietly wrong by a factor of two.
WHY IT HAPPENED (root cause)
  The gate trigger fired on both the leading edge and the trailing edge of the crossing - the code treated entering and leaving the gate as two separate events. WHAT HAPPENED
  The robot shuffled against a wall for nine seconds, reversing 0.2s and advancing 0.2s forever. Both motions worked; the combination was useless.

E0839 | v7.9 | BIG | Found Day 140 | Fixed in 4 days | Pi SSH terminal

  $ python3 checkpoint.py

  race cannot finish
WHAT HAPPENED
  The robot stopped exactly on the lap line and the counter refused to advance. The robot was on the line - why did the count not register?

  callback ran twice per tick
  motor command overwritten
WHAT HAPPENED
  Every control tick produced two motor commands, the second overwriting the first. The motion was erratic because half the commands were stale by one tick.

  register_task was called twice for the same task ID in main - once by the module's own registration and once by the application wiring. WHAT HAPPENED
  Critical failures appeared in the log with the INFO level, so nobody noticed them in the morning's flood of messages. The logging was lying about importance.
